game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 3 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Before anything is revealed, fair value is 10.5 (three dice at 3.5 each), with a standard deviation of about 2.96.

**Choosing the spread.** For each candidate ask, I compared:
- the expected gain from noise traders who buy above it, and
- the expected loss to informed traders when the true sum is above it.

| Ask | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net per side |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12.5 | ≈0.42 | ≈0.16 | ≈0.26 |
| 13.0 | ≈0.46 | ≈0.11 | ≈0.35 |
| 13.5 | ≈0.48 | ≈0.09 | ≈0.40 |
| 14.0 | ≈0.49 | ≈0.06 | ≈0.43 |
| 14.5 | ≈0.47 | ≈0.04 | ≈0.43 |

The net edge peaks at around 3.5 to 4 points from fair. An ask of exactly 14.0 works well because an informed trader with a sum of 14 is not above the ask, so it won't buy. The bid side is symmetric, giving a bid of 7.0.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 14.0}

Before anything is revealed, the fair value is the expected sum of three dice: 3 × 3.5 = **10.5**. The sum has a standard deviation of about 2.96. The previous quote of 7/14 drew no trade, which tells us almost nothing, so fair value stays at 10.5.

**Choosing the spread.** For an ask at 10.5 + h, the expected profit per quote is:
- the gain from noise traders: 0.65 × P(noise > h) × h, where the noise has standard deviation 4.4;
- minus the loss to informed traders: 0.35 × E[(V − ask)⁺], using the exact distribution of the three-dice sum.

| Ask | Gain from noise | Loss to informed | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12.5 | 0.42 | 0.16 | 0.26 |
| 13.5 | 0.48 | 0.085 | 0.40 |
| 14.0 | 0.485 | 0.057 | 0.43 |
| 14.5 | 0.473 | 0.040 | **0.433** |
| 15.0 | 0.448 | 0.024 | 0.42 |

The best ask is about 14.5. The distribution is symmetric around 10.5, so the matching bid is 6.5.

{"bid": 6.5, "ask": 14.5}

Die 1 shows 4, so the remaining two dice sum to 7 on average. That makes the public fair value 4 + 7 = **11**. The earlier no-trade quotes were symmetric, so they don't shift it.

To set the ask, write it as 11 + d. For each d, I compared the expected gain from noise traders with the expected loss to informed traders, using the exact two-dice distribution. The bid side is the mirror image.

| d | Expected net per side |
|---|---|
| 3.0 | ≈ 0.44 |
| 3.5 | ≈ 0.46 |
| 3.8 | ≈ 0.46 |
| 4.0 | ≈ 0.46 |
| 4.5 | ≈ 0.44 |

The best range is d ≈ 3.8–4, so I quote d = 3.9 on both sides, giving a bid of 7.1 and an ask of 14.9.

{"bid": 7.1, "ask": 14.9}

Die 1 is 4 and the other two dice average 7, so the public fair value is 11. The two hidden dice add 2.4 of standard deviation to the settlement value.

To set the spread, I weighed two effects on each side:
- **Noise traders:** a wider spread earns more per trade but trades less often.
- **Informed traders:** they only trade when the true value is beyond my quote, so a wider spread loses less to them.

Expected profit per side is roughly flat for half-spreads between about 3.5 and 4, at around 0.46 per side. I'll keep a half-spread of about 3.8 around 11.

{"bid": 7.2, "ask": 14.8}

With dice 1 and 2 known (4 + 6 = 10), the settlement is 10 plus die 3, so it is equally likely to be any whole number from 11 to 16. The public fair value is 13.5.

**Ask side.** An informed trader can value the contract at 16 at most.
- Any ask of 16 or higher is never hit by an informed buyer.
- So above 16, profit comes only from noise traders. Their valuations are 13.5 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 4.4.
- Expected profit is 0.65 × (ask − 13.5) × P(noise valuation > ask).

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 16.0 | ≈ 0.46 |
| 16.8 | ≈ 0.486 |
| 17.0 | ≈ 0.485 |
| 18.0 | ≈ 0.45 |

The best ask is about 16.8.

**Bid side.** The problem is symmetric around 13.5, so the best bid is 13.5 − 3.3 = 10.2. That is below the lowest possible settlement of 11, so informed traders never sell to me there.

My position limits are not a constraint here, and holding inventory does not change expected profit.

{"bid": 10.2, "ask": 16.8}

Die 1 (4) and die 2 (6) are known, and die 3 is still uniform on 1–6. That makes the fair value 4 + 6 + 3.5 = **13.5**, and the settlement value must lie between 11 and 16.

**Informed traders.**
- If my ask is at least 16, an informed trader never buys, because the value cannot exceed 16.
- If my bid is at most 11, an informed trader never sells, because the value cannot fall below 11.

**Noise traders.** Their valuation is 13.5 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 4.4.
- With an ask at 13.5 + d, my expected profit from them is 0.65 × P(noise > d) × d.
- This is largest at d ≈ 0.75 × 4.4 ≈ 3.3, giving about 0.49 per side.
- An ask of 13.5 + 3.3 = 16.8 is above 16, so informed traders never buy.
- A bid of 13.5 − 3.3 = 10.2 is below 11, so informed traders never sell.

Both sides lose nothing to informed traders while earning the most from noise traders.

{"bid": 10.2, "ask": 16.8}

game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
- Die 3 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Before any dice are revealed, the expected sum is 3 × 3.5 = 10.5, with a standard deviation of about 2.96.

I compared spreads by weighing what I earn from noise traders against what I lose to informed traders:

| Half-spread | Net expected profit per side |
|---|---|
| 2 | ≈ 0.26 |
| 3 | ≈ 0.40 |
| 3.5 | ≈ 0.43 |
| 4 | ≈ 0.43 |
| 4.5 | ≈ 0.42 |

A half-spread of about 4 is close to the best, so I quote 6.5 / 14.5.

{"bid": 6.5, "ask": 14.5}

Public fair value after quote 1 is about 9.4 (prior was 10.5). Being long 1, I shade my quotes slightly lower and keep a band of roughly ±2 around it.

- **Before trading:** the sum of three dice has mean 10.5 and standard deviation about 2.96.
- **What the sale at 6.5 implies:**
  - An informed trader sells only if the sum is 6 or less. That has probability 20/216 ≈ 0.093, and the average sum in that case is 5.25.
  - A noise trader sells if 10.5 plus noise falls below 6.5. That has probability Φ(−4/4.4) ≈ 0.18.
- **Updated estimate:**
  - The noise-trader route carries weight 0.65 × 0.18 ≈ 0.118 and leaves the expected sum at 10.5.
  - The informed route carries weight 0.35 × 0.093 ≈ 0.032 and points to 5.25.
  - The weighted average gives a fair value of about 9.37.

{"bid": 7.3, "ask": 11.2}

Die 1 = 5, so the remaining two dice average 7, which gives a prior fair value of 12.

**Updating on the stage-1 trades**
- **Sale at 6.5:** An informed seller would only sell there if the sum were 6 or less. With die 1 = 5, the sum is at least 7, so this seller must have been noise. That trade tells us nothing new.
- **Purchase at 11.2:** An informed buyer would only buy there if the sum were 12 or more. That means dice 2 and 3 sum to 7 or more.
  - Chance of that, before the trade: 21/36.
  - Chance a noise trader buys at 11.2, with public fair value about 10.5: about 0.44.
  - Chance of the buy if the two dice sum to 7 or more: 0.35 + 0.65 × 0.44 ≈ 0.63. If they sum to less: about 0.28.
  - Average of the two dice if they sum to 7 or more: 182/21 ≈ 8.67. If less: 70/15 ≈ 4.67.
  - Combining these, the expected sum of dice 2 and 3 is about 7.7. So fair value is about 12.7.

**Quote**
I set a spread of roughly ±1.8 around 12.7. The remaining uncertainty is a standard deviation of about 2.4, and informed traders are a real risk.

{"bid": 10.9, "ask": 14.5}

Die 1 came up 5, so before any trading the fair value is 5 + 3.5 + 3.5 = 12.

**Updating on quote 3.** Someone sold to me at 10.9.
- A noise trader values the contract at 12 plus noise, so it sells at 10.9 with probability about Φ(−1.1/4.4) ≈ 0.40.
- An informed trader sells only if the true value is 10 or less. That means dice 2 and 3 sum to 5 or less, which has probability 10/36.

Weighting these by how likely each trader type is:
- The chance that dice 2 and 3 sum to 5 or less rises to about 0.47.
- In that case the sum of dice 2 and 3 averages 4.
- Otherwise it averages about 8.15.
- So the expected sum of dice 2 and 3 is about 6.19, and fair value is about **11.2**.

**Quote check** (I am long 1, so I lean slightly lower):
- **Ask 12.5.**
  - An informed trader buys if the value is 13 or more, about 30% likely. Those buys cost me roughly 1.8 each, an expected −0.19 per quote.
  - Noise traders buy about 25% of the time and earn me 1.3 each, an expected +0.33.
  - Net: about +0.13.
- **Bid 9.9.**
  - An informed trader sells if the value is 9 or less, about 28% likely. Those sales cost me roughly 1.6 each, an expected −0.16.
  - Noise traders sell about 26% of the time and earn me 1.3 each, an expected +0.33.
  - Net: about +0.18.

Both sides have positive expected profit.

{"bid": 9.9, "ask": 12.5}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed (5 + 4 = 9), so the settlement value is 9 plus die 3. That makes it uniform on 10–15, with expected value 12.5.

**Pricing against informed traders.** An informed counterparty only trades when your price is wrong relative to the true value. Any ask at or above 15 and any bid at or below 10 can never be picked off. Quoting inside that range adds some chance of an informed trade against you.

**Pricing for noise traders.** Noise traders value the contract at 12.5 plus noise with standard deviation 4.4. With probability 0.65 the counterparty is a noise trader, so the expected profit on the ask side is 0.65 × P(noise > ask − 12.5) × (ask − 12.5):

| Ask | Edge over 12.5 | P(noise trader buys) | Expected profit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 2.5 | 0.285 | ≈ 0.46 |
| 16 | 3.5 | 0.213 | ≈ 0.49 (best) |
| 17 | 4.5 | 0.153 | ≈ 0.45 |

Tighter asks do worse because informed losses outweigh the extra noise volume. At 14.1 the expected profit is about 0.32, and at 13.1 it is negative.

The bid side is symmetric around 12.5, so the best bid is about 9.0.

{"bid": 9.0, "ask": 16.0}

Dice 1 and 2 total 9 (5 + 4). Die 3 is uniform on 1 to 6, so the contract settles somewhere in 10 to 15. The fair value is 12.5. My last quote of 9 / 16 drew no trade, which tells us nothing new.

**What each type of counterparty does**
- An informed trader buys only if the settlement value is above my ask. It sells only if the value is below my bid.
- If my ask is at least 15, an informed trader can never profitably buy. If my bid is at most 10, it can never profitably sell.
- So with an ask of 15 or more and a bid of 10 or less, the informed trader never trades against me. All remaining profit comes from noise traders, whose valuations are 12.5 plus noise with standard deviation 4.4.

**Choosing the distance from fair value**
- Quoting d away from 12.5, I earn about 0.65 × d × P(noise exceeds d) on each side.
- This peaks at roughly d = 3.4:
  - d = 2.5 gives about 0.463.
  - d = 3.0 gives about 0.483.
  - d = 3.4 gives about 0.486.
  - d = 4.0 gives about 0.472.
- Moving inside 15 on the ask (for example to 14) lets the informed trader buy when the value is 15. That lowers the expected profit to about 0.30.

So I quote about 3.4 either side of 12.5.

{"bid": 9.1, "ask": 15.9}

info.raw:

For an ask set s above fair value, my expected profit is two parts. Noise traders buy with probability P(N(0,3) > s), and I gain s on each of those trades. Informed traders cost me E[(V − ask)⁺], where V is the settlement value.

Expected profit per quote, by ask level:

| Ask | Gain from noise traders | Loss to informed traders | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12.5 | 0.328 | 0.159 | ≈ 0.169 |
| 13.0 | 0.33 | 0.113 | ≈ 0.22 |

Fair value is 10.5, the expected sum of three dice. The quote at 7.5 / 13.5 drew no trade, which hints the sum is mid-range but doesn't move the fair value, because the evidence is symmetric around 10.5.

I compared expected profit per quote at different half-spreads. For each, I weighed what I earn from noise traders (65%) against what I lose to informed traders (35%), using the exact distribution of the dice sum:
- **Half-spread 2 (ask 12.5):** about 0.17 per side.
- **Half-spread 3 (ask 13.5):** about 0.22 per side.

No trades so far, so the fair value stays at 10.5, the expected sum of three dice. For an ask half-spread h around 10.5, my expected profit per quote is the noise traders' gain minus the informed traders' loss:

| Ask | Noise gain | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12.5 (h = 2) | +0.328 | −0.159 | 0.169 |

- **Noise gain:** 0.65 × P(noise valuation > ask) × h, with noise standard deviation 3.

{"bid": 7.5, "ask": 13.5}

Die 1 came up 1, so the fair value is 1 + 3.5 + 3.5 = 8. The two unrevealed dice can take the sum anywhere from 3 to 13.

I compared expected profit per quote for different half-spreads around 8:

|---|---|

A half-spread of about 3 is best. A wider spread loses less to informed traders but trades less often with noise traders. So I quote 5.0 / 11.0.

Die 1 came up 1, so the fair value is 1 + 3.5 + 3.5 = **8**. The other two dice sum to 2–12, with a standard deviation of about 2.4.

The last quote (5 / 11) got no trade. An informed trader would only have traded if the total were below 5 or above 11. Those two cases are equally likely (3/36 each), so no trade leaves the fair value at 8.

I picked the half-spread h around 8 to balance profit from noise traders against losses to informed traders, per side, per quote:

| h | Expected profit from noise traders | Expected loss to informed traders | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | 0.328 | 0.097 | 0.231 |
| 2.5 | 0.329 | 0.068 | 0.261 |
| 3.0 | 0.310 | 0.039 | **0.271** |
| 3.5 | 0.277 | 0.024 | 0.253 |

A half-spread of 3 does best, so I quote 5 / 11 again.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 11}

Die 1 showed 1, and dice 2 and 3 are still unknown with an expected sum of 7. So fair value is 1 + 7 = 8. The two quotes at 5/11 with no trade give no reason to shift this, because the evidence they carry is symmetric around 8.

The quotes should sit 3 either side of fair value. I set the ask by weighing the edge from noise traders against the expected loss to informed traders, and the bid is symmetric:

| Ask | Expected net edge per quote |
|---|---|
| 9 | about +0.05 |
| 10 | about +0.23 |
| 10.5 | about +0.26 |
| 11 | about +0.27 |
| 11.5 | about +0.25 |

An ask of 11 gives the best expected edge, so I keep the quote at 5/11.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 11}

With dice 1 and 2 revealed, the known part of the sum is 1 + 6 = 7. Die 3 is still hidden, so the settlement value is 8 to 13, each equally likely. The fair value is 10.5. The last quote (8 / 13) didn't trade, which tells us almost nothing new.

To choose the ask, I compared expected profit per quote at a few prices:
- **Ask 13:** no informed trader ever buys, because the value can't exceed 13. A noise trader buys about 20% of the time (valuation above 13). That gives 0.65 × 2.5 × 0.20 ≈ 0.33.
- **Ask 12.5:** an informed trader buys when the value is 13, which loses a little. Total is about 0.30.
- **Ask 13.5:** total is about 0.31.

So an ask of 13 is about optimal. The game is symmetric around 10.5, so the same reasoning puts the best bid at 8.

{"bid": 8, "ask": 13}

**Fair value.** Dice 1 and 2 are known (1 + 6 = 7). Die 3 is uniform on 1–6, so the settlement value is uniform on 8–13. The public fair value is 10.5. This is the last quote, so I only need to maximise the expected profit of this one trade.

**Choosing the ask.** I compared expected profit at several ask prices. Noise traders value the contract at 10.5 + N(0, 3), and informed traders buy only when the true value is strictly above my ask.

| Ask | Gain from noise buyers | Loss to informed buyers | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12.0 | 0.65 × 0.309 × 1.5 ≈ 0.301 | 0.35 × (1/6) × 1 ≈ 0.058 | ≈ 0.24 |
| 12.5 | 0.65 × 0.252 × 2.0 ≈ 0.328 | ≈ 0.029 | ≈ 0.30 |
| 12.9 | 0.65 × 0.212 × 2.4 ≈ 0.331 | ≈ 0.006 | ≈ 0.325 |
| 13.0 | 0.65 × 0.202 × 2.5 ≈ 0.329 | 0 | ≈ 0.33 |
| 13.1 | ≈ 0.326 | 0 | ≈ 0.326 |
| 13.5 | ≈ 0.309 | 0 | ≈ 0.31 |

At 13.0 an informed trader never buys, because the highest possible value is 13 and that is not above my ask. Net profit peaks at about 13.0.

**Choosing the bid.** The problem is symmetric around 10.5, so the best bid is 8.0. At that price an informed trader never sells, because the lowest possible value is 8.

Fair value is about 9.7. That is my estimate of the expected settlement value given the trades so far.

**How I got there:**
- **Prior:** the sum of three dice has mean 10.5 and standard deviation about 2.96.
- **Quote 1 (sold at 8):** a sale at my bid is more likely when the true sum is 7 or less. An informed seller only sells then, and a noise seller does so about 20% of the time. Updating on this lowers the fair value to about 9.74.
- **Quote 2 (no trade at 7.8 / 11.4):** no trade is somewhat more likely when the sum is 8 to 11, because an informed trader would then do nothing. This barely moves the estimate, leaving it at about 9.72.

**My quote:**
- I keep a spread of roughly ±1.5 to 2 around 9.7 to protect against informed traders, since the value is still very uncertain.
- I am long 1 unit, so I shade the quote slightly lower. This makes selling a bit more likely than buying, which would reduce my position.

{"bid": 7.8, "ask": 11.2}

With die 1 revealed as 5, the expected settlement is 5 + 7 = 12. The sale at 8 in stage 1 hints that the hidden dice may be slightly low, so I put fair value a little under 12, around 11.8–12.

I compared, for each ask, the expected edge from noise traders against the expected loss to informed traders:
- **Ask 13:** net expected profit about 0.18 per quote.
- **Ask 14:** about 0.35.
- **Ask 14.5:** about 0.37, the best of those checked.
- **Ask 15:** about 0.36.

The bid side is roughly symmetric, so the best bid is near 9.5. I am long 1 and fair value leans slightly low, so I shade both sides down a little.

{"bid": 9.4, "ask": 14.3}

Die 1 is 5, so the expected sum is 5 + 7 = 12. The earlier trades barely change this, so I treat public fair value as about 12.

**Ask.** I compared the gain from noise buyers with the expected loss to informed buyers at several ask levels:

| Ask | Gain from noise buyers | Loss to informed buyers | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 13.5 | 0.37 | 0.08 | ≈ 0.29 |
| 14.0 | 0.40 | 0.06 | ≈ 0.35 |
| 14.5 | 0.40 | 0.04 | ≈ 0.365 |
| 15.0 | 0.38 | 0.02 | ≈ 0.36 |

The best ask is around 14.5, which is 2.5 above fair value.

**Bid.** By symmetry the best bid is about 9.5.

**Position.** I am long 1, so I lean the quotes slightly lower: bid 9.5, ask 14.4.

{"bid": 9.5, "ask": 14.4}

Die 1 shows 5. The other two dice sum to 7 on average, so fair value is about 12 (range 7–17). The two quotes with no trade this stage tell me very little.

I chose how far the ask sits above fair value by trading off two effects on expected profit:
- **Noise traders:** a wider ask means fewer of them buy from me, but each sale earns more.
- **Informed traders:** a wider ask means fewer of them pick me off when the true value is above my ask.

| Ask offset above 12 | Expected profit per quote |
|---|---|
| 1.5 | about 0.29 |
| 2.0 | about 0.35 |
| 2.5 | about 0.37 (best) |
| 3.0 | about 0.36 |

The best offset is about 2.5. The bid works the same way, since the distribution is symmetric. I'm long 1, so I set the ask slightly tighter to make selling a little more likely.

{"bid": 9.5, "ask": 14.4}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed as 5 and 6, so they sum to 11. Die 3 is uniform from 1 to 6. The contract will therefore settle at a value from 12 to 17, and the expected value is 14.5. My long position of +1 is well within the limits, so I'll quote symmetrically around 14.5.

**Ask:** the expected profit at a given ask level is
0.8 × P(noise trader values it above the ask) × (ask − 14.5), plus 0.2 × the expected loss to an informed trader.
- Ask 16.0: about 0.34
- Ask 16.9: about 0.40
- Ask 17.0: about 0.405, the best of these. No informed trader would buy here, because the value cannot exceed 17.
- Ask 17.2: about 0.40
- Ask 17.5: about 0.38

**Bid:** by symmetry the best bid is 12.0, where no informed trader would sell because the value cannot be below 12.

{"bid": 12.0, "ask": 17.0}

Dice 1 and 2 are known (5 + 6 = 11), so the contract settles at 11 plus die 3. That makes it a value between 12 and 17, each equally likely, with a fair value of 14.5.

**Ask:** I want the ask that maximises expected profit per quote. Noise traders value the contract at 14.5 plus Normal noise with standard deviation 3. Informed traders know the true value, which is one of 12 to 17.
- At 17.0, noise traders buy about 20% of the time and pay me about 2.5 above fair value. An informed trader never buys, because no value is above 17. Expected profit is about 0.405.
- At 16.0, expected profit is only about 0.34, because an informed trader would buy when the value is 17.
- At 17.5, expected profit drops to about 0.38, because fewer noise traders buy.
- So 17.0 is roughly the best ask.

**Bid:** The same reasoning applies on the other side, so the best bid is 12.0. Holding +1 doesn't change this, because I only care about expected profit, not risk.

{"bid": 12.0, "ask": 17.0}

Die 1 and die 2 are known: 5 + 6 = 11. The settlement value is 11 + die 3, so it lies between 12 and 17. The expected value is 14.5.

The history adds no information about die 3:
- **Quote 7 (12 / 17, no trade):** an informed trader would not trade at these prices for any possible value, so the lack of a trade says nothing.
- **Quote 8 (bought at 17):** an informed trader buys only if the value is above 17, which is impossible. That trade must have come from a noise trader.

So the public fair value stays at 14.5.

**Choosing the ask.** An ask of 17 can never be hit by an informed trader. The expected profit from noise buyers is 0.8 × P(Z > 0.833) × 2.5 ≈ 0.405. Asks slightly above or below 17 give the same or lower expected profit.

**Choosing the bid.** The bid is the mirror case. A bid of 12 can never be hit by an informed trader, and its expected profit is also about 0.405.

{"bid": 12, "ask": 17}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 4, 10.
- Die 2 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value with nothing revealed is the sum of the three dice means: 3.75 + 2.5 + 6.25 = 12.5. The standard deviation of the total is about 5.8. Half the counterparties are informed, so I quote a wide spread of about ±4 around fair value to limit losses to them.

{"bid": 8.5, "ask": 16.5}

Before any trade, the expected sum is 3.75 + 2.5 + 6.25 = 12.5.

**What the first trade tells me.** Someone bought at 16.5, which is evidence the sum is high.
- The sum is at least 17 with probability 70/256 ≈ 0.27.
- When the sum is that high, its average is about 19.9.
- A noise trader values above 16.5 with probability about 0.25.

Updating on the buy moves my fair value to about 16.4. Most of that weight comes from the case where die 1 rolled 10.

**Quote.** I centre the quote near the updated fair value. I keep it wide because informed traders are likely and the distribution is lumpy. I lean the ask slightly higher because I'm already short 1.

{"bid": 12.5, "ask": 21.0}

Fair value estimate:
- **Prior:** The expected sum is 3.75 + 2.5 + 6.25 = 12.5, with a standard deviation of about 5.8.
- **Quote 1:** Someone bought at 16.5. An informed trader buys there only if the sum is above 16.5, so the estimate rises. Updated on that buy, fair value is about 16.
- **Quote 2:** Nobody traded at 12.5 / 21. That rules out an informed trader with a sum above 21 or below 12.5.
- **Combined:** Putting both quotes together, fair value is about 16.5–17.

Since half the counterparties are informed, I keep the spread wide. I'm short one unit, so I lean the quote slightly upward around a fair value near 17.

{"bid": 14, "ask": 21}

Die 1 = 10, so the settlement value is 10 plus die 2 plus die 3.

**Prior fair value.** Die 2 averages 2.5 and die 3 averages 6.25, so the prior fair value is 18.75.

**Updating on the trading history.** I weighted each possible die 2 + die 3 sum by how likely it made the three trade outcomes. I assumed noise traders were centred near the fair value at the time, about 12.5 to 14.5.
- The buy at 16.5 points to a high sum (7 or more).
- No one traded at 12.5/21 or 14/21. Informed traders stay out only if the value is inside the quote, so this points to a sum between 4 and 11.

The posterior puts most of the value between 17 and 21, with a mean of about 19.0. Values of 16 or less, or 22 or more, are each only a few percent likely.

**Choosing the quote.** Because the value is so concentrated, a wide quote rarely loses to informed traders. Noise traders, with a spread of 5.8 around the fair value, still cross a wide quote fairly often.
- Ask: expected profit rises from about 0.08 at 20.1 to about 0.4 at 22 and about 0.5 at 23.
- Bid: around 15 to 16 looks best.
- I am short one unit, so I lean the quote slightly toward buying.

{"bid": 15.6, "ask": 22.8}

Fair value is about 19.0, and the bid of 17.2 and ask of 21.2 sit just outside where the value most likely lies.

**Prior given the reveal (die 1 = 10):**
- Die 2 averages 2.5 and die 3 averages 6.25.
- So the prior fair value is 10 + 8.75 = 18.75.

**What the trading history adds:**
- **Quote 1:** The buy at 16.5 makes it more likely that die 2 + die 3 is above 6.5 (likelihood ratio about 5 to 1).
- **Quotes 2–4:** These had no trade, so an informed trader probably valued the contract inside those quotes. That favours die 2 + die 3 roughly between 5.6 and 11.

I weighted all 64 combinations of die 2 and die 3 by these trade and no-trade likelihoods. The result:
- Die 2 + die 3 has a posterior mean of about 9.0, so fair value is about 19.0.
- About 95% of the weight is on die 2 + die 3 between 7 and 11, a settlement value of 17 to 21.

**Choosing the quote:**
- An informed trader will rarely trade against quotes just outside 17–21.
- Noise traders (valuation around 19, standard deviation 5.8) still trade with about 38% probability on each side.
- Bid 17.2: the only informed loss is if the value is exactly 17, which costs 0.2. Against that, noise sellers give an edge of about 1.8.
- Ask 21.2: this is above the most likely values, so a buyer there is mostly noise.

{"bid": 17.2, "ask": 21.2}

Die 1 is revealed as 10, so the value is 10 plus die 2 plus die 3. With no trading history the expected value would be 10 + 2.5 + 6.25 = 18.75.

**What the trading history tells me**
- At quote 1, someone bought at my ask of 16.5. That makes a value above 16.5 more likely.
- At quotes 2 and 3 there was no trade at my asks of 21. That makes a value of 21 or below more likely.
- In stage 2, there was no trade at 15.6–22.8 or at 17.2–21.2. That points strongly to a value between 18 and 21.

**Posterior estimate**
- The likely values are 18 (about 25%), 19 (about 35%), 20 (about 13%) and 21 (about 22%).
- Values outside 17 to 22 are very unlikely.
- The posterior expected value is about 19.2.

**Choosing the quotes**
- An ask above 21 is never hit by an informed trader holding a likely value (18 to 21). It only trades with noise traders, and pushing it to about 3 above fair value earns the most from them.
- On the same logic, a bid at or below 17 is almost never hit by an informed trader. Setting it about 3 below fair value earns the most from noise traders.

{"bid": 16.0, "ask": 22.5}

Die 1 = 10 and die 3 = 8 are revealed, so 18 is locked in. Die 2 is still unknown, with faces 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9. That makes the settlement 18 (3/8), 19 (1/8), 20 (1/8), 22 (2/8) or 27 (1/8). The mean is 20.5, which is the public fair value.

**Ask side:** An ask of 27 or higher is never lifted by an informed trader, because the most the contract can settle at is 27. A noise trader values it at 20.5 plus noise with standard deviation 5.8, so it sometimes still buys. At 27 the expected edge is about 0.43, which is the highest I found for the ask.

**Bid side:** A bid of 18 or lower is never hit by an informed trader, because the least the contract can settle at is 18. Going lower trades less often but earns more per trade. Expected noise edge is about 0.42 at 18, 0.48 at 17, 0.49 at 16 and 0.47 at 15. So a bid near 16 is best.

My position of -1 doesn't come close to any limit, so I quote both sides.

{"bid": 16, "ask": 27}

**Fair value estimate**

- Dice 1 and 3 are revealed: 10 + 8 = 18. So settlement = 18 + die 2.
- Die 2 can be 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4 or 9, so settlement is in {18, 18, 18, 19, 20, 22, 22, 27}.
- The trading history makes high die-2 values unlikely:
  - An informed trader holding 22 or 27 would have bought at the asks of 21 (quotes 2 and 3) and 21.2 (quote 5).
  - An informed trader holding 27 would also have bought at 22.8 and 22.5 (quotes 4 and 6).
  - None of those trades happened.
- Weighting the outcomes by how likely each one makes this history, settlement is about 18 (60%), 19 (20%) or 20 (20%). The chance of 22 or 27 is under 1%.
- That gives a public fair value of about 18.6.

**Quote choice**

- **Ask:** Informed buyers can almost never profit above about 20. So the ask only needs to balance edge against noise-trader fill rate (noise is N(18.6, 5.8)). This peaks near 23.
- **Bid:** Any bid above 18 gets hit by informed sellers holding 18, which is costly. Below 18, the trade-off between noise fill rate and edge peaks around 14 to 14.5.

{"bid": 14.5, "ask": 22.9}

Die 1 = 10 and die 3 = 8 are known, so settlement is 18 plus die 2. Die 2 is one of 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9, so settlement can be 18, 19, 20, 22 or 27.

**Updating the fair value from quote 8.** Quote 8 was bid 14.5 and ask 22.9 with no trade. An informed trader holding 27 would have bought at 22.9, so the lack of a trade makes 27 less likely.
- A noise trader trades nothing about half the time at those quotes. So the chance of no trade is about 0.25 if the value is 27 and about 0.75 for any other value.
- After this update the probabilities are:
  - 18: about 41%
  - 19: about 14%
  - 20: about 14%
  - 22: about 27%
  - 27: about 5%
- That gives a fair value of about 19.9.

**Choosing the bid.** The bid should stay at 18 or lower, so informed sellers never trade against me. Below that, I balance how often noise traders sell to me against the edge I earn on each trade. Expected profit is about 0.49 for a bid anywhere from 15 to 16, which is the best range.

**Choosing the ask.** The only informed buyer who hurts me holds 27, and that has a small probability. Expected profit is about 0.44 for an ask near 25, which is the best level.

{"bid": 15.5, "ask": 25}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.
- Die 2 (8 faces, loaded): 1 (prob 1/10), 1 (prob 1/10), 1 (prob 1/10), 7 (prob 1/10), 9 (prob 1/5), 9 (prob 1/5), 11 (prob 1/10), 11 (prob 1/10).
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 3, 3, 3, 5, 6, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Expected settlement value with nothing revealed:

- **Die 1:** the eight faces sum to 54, so the expected value is 6.75 (variance about 19.4).
- **Die 2:** 0.3×1 + 0.1×7 + 0.4×9 + 0.2×11 = 6.8 (variance about 15.6).
- **Die 3:** the eight faces sum to 39, so the expected value is 4.875 (variance about 7.6).
- **Total:** the expected sum is about 18.4, with a standard deviation of about 6.5.

**Spread:** Informed traders see the true value, which is spread about 6.5 around the fair value. Noise traders' valuations are also spread 6.5 around it. Treating both as roughly normal, the best half-spread is about 1.2 standard deviations. That is roughly ±7.8 around 18.4. The true value isn't exactly normal, so this is an approximation.

{"bid": 10.6, "ask": 26.2}

**Fair value.** The contract is the sum of three independent dice, so the expected value and variance just add up:

| Die | Mean | Variance |
|---|---|---|
| Die 1 | 6.75 | 19.44 |
| Die 2 | 6.8 | 15.56 |
| Die 3 | 4.875 | 7.61 |
| **Total** | **18.425** | **42.6** (s.d. about 6.5) |

**Effect of quote 1.** Quote 1 at 10.6/26.2 produced no trade. That tells us little, and both sides were about equally far from fair, so fair value stays about 18.4.

**Choosing the spread.** I treat both the informed trader's valuation and the noise trader's valuation as roughly Normal around 18.4 with s.d. 6.5. For a half-spread h, each side of the quote earns about h × P(trade) from noise traders and loses the expected informed overshoot.

| Half-spread h | Expected profit per side |
|---|---|
| 5.5 | about 0.19 |
| 7.8 | about 0.27 |
| 9.75 | about 0.23 |

So the best half-spread is around 7.5–8. I'll quote symmetrically around 18.4 with a half-spread of about 7.6.

{"bid": 10.8, "ask": 26.0}

Expected settlement value with nothing revealed:
- Die 1 has mean 6.75 and variance about 19.4.
- Die 2 has mean 6.8 and variance about 15.6.
- Die 3 has mean 4.875 and variance about 7.6.
- The total has mean about 18.4 and standard deviation about 6.5.

The two earlier quotes were roughly symmetric around this value and did not trade, so the fair value stays near 18.4.

To set the spread, I treat both the informed and noise valuations as roughly Normal around 18.4 with standard deviation 6.5. The expected profit per side is proportional to 2z·Q(z) − φ(z), where z is the half-spread divided by 6.5. This peaks near z ≈ 1.1–1.2, a half-spread of about 7.3–7.5. The distribution is somewhat skewed, so this is approximate. I keep the quotes about the same as before, slightly tighter.

{"bid": 11.0, "ask": 25.8}

Fair value is about 9.4. Before the stage-1 sale it would have been 14.55, but the sale at 11 pulls it down.

**Fair value**
- **Unconditional means:**
  - Die 1: 54/8 = 6.75.
  - Die 2: 0.3×1 + 0.1×7 + 0.4×9 + 0.2×11 = 6.8.
  - Die 3: revealed as 1.
  - Total: 14.55.
- **Updating on the sale at 11 in quote 3:**
  - An informed trader sells at 11 only if the sum is below 11. With die 3 = 1, that means die 1 + die 2 < 10.
  - In stage 1 the public fair value was about 18.4. A noise trader values the contract below 11 with probability about 0.13.
  - Conditioning on the sale gives about a 72% chance that die 1 + die 2 is below 10 (average 5.5 in that case). The other 28% averages about 15.9.
  - Fair ≈ 0.72×5.5 + 0.28×15.9 + 1 ≈ 9.4.

**Posterior distribution of the settlement value**
- The low cluster has values 2, 3 and 5 at about 0.12 each, 8 and 9 at about 0.04 each, and 10 at about 0.28.
- The high cluster spreads from 11 to 24, with about 0.28 total probability.

**Choosing the quote**
- **Ask:** I balanced noise-trader edge (a buyer at ask a gives me a − 9.4) against losses to informed traders when the value exceeds the ask. Expected profit peaks around an ask of 18–20, at about +0.2 per quote.
- **Bid:** No posterior value lies between 3 and 5, so a bid of 3 barely loses to informed sellers. Noise sellers there give an edge of about 6.4. Expected profit is about +0.46 per quote.

{"bid": 3.0, "ask": 18.0}

The public fair value is about 9.4, and I'm skewing slightly toward selling because I'm long.

**Starting expectations**
- Die 1 has a mean of 54/8 = 6.75.
- Die 2 has a mean of 0.3·1 + 0.1·7 + 0.4·9 + 0.2·11 = 6.8.
- Die 3 is revealed as 1.
- With no trade information, the expected sum would be about 14.55.

**What the stage-1 sale at 11 tells us**
- Given die 3 = 1, the settlement is below 11 only when die 1 + die 2 < 10. That has probability 0.225.
- In that low case, die 1 + die 2 averages about 5.5. Otherwise it averages about 15.9.
- An informed trader always sells at 11 when the value is below 11. A noise trader sells there with probability about 0.127, because the stage-1 fair value was about 18.4.
- So the sale was likely with probability about 0.56 in the low case and 0.06 in the high case.
- That shifts the probability of the low case to about 0.72.
- The posterior expected sum is 0.72·5.5 + 0.28·15.9 + 1 ≈ 9.4.
- Quote 4 (bid 3, ask 18, no trade) barely changes this.

**Setting the quote**
- The settlement distribution is wide and lumpy, so I'm keeping a fairly wide spread to protect against informed traders.
- Because I'm long 1, I'm leaning the quote slightly toward selling.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 13}

Fair value is about 12.1. I'm quoting bid 9.5 and ask 14.

1. **Prior.** With die 3 = 1, the expected settlement is 1 + 6.75 (die 1) + 6.8 (die 2) = 14.55.

2. **What the two quiet quotes tell me.**
   - At quote 4 (3 / 18), an informed trader would trade only if the value were outside 3–18.
   - At quote 5 (5 / 13), an informed trader would trade only if the value were outside 5–13.
   - A noise trader would have stayed out of both with probability of roughly 0.66 × 0.34 ≈ 0.22.
   - So the chance of two quiet quotes is about 0.61 if the value is between 5 and 13, and about 0.11 otherwise.

3. **Updated fair value.**
   - Before the update, the value lies between 5 and 13 with probability 0.425, with average 10.8 there.
   - Otherwise (probability 0.575) its average is about 17.3.
   - Weighting by the chances above gives about 0.80 for the 5–13 range and about 0.20 for outside it.
   - The updated fair value is about 12.1.

4. **Quote.**
   - The likely settlement values cluster at 10–13.
   - I quote around fair, with the ask above 13 so I don't sell to informed traders when the value is high.
   - I shade both sides slightly down because I'm already long one unit.

{"bid": 9.5, "ask": 14}

The settlement value is 2 plus die 1, so I quote a low bid and a high ask around a fair value of about 10.7.

**Known so far.** Dice 2 and 3 both show 1. So the settlement is die 1 + 2, which can be 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13 or 14, each equally likely before using the trading history.

**What the history says about die 1.**
- At quote 3, a counterparty sold to me at 11. An informed trader does that only if the total is below 11, so this favours a low die 1.
- There were no trades at quotes 1, 2 and 4–6. An informed trader holding a total of 2, 3 or 5 would have sold at those bids. An informed trader holding a total of 14 would have bought at my ask of 13 at quote 5. Neither happened, so those values are less likely.
- Combining these, my rough posterior for the total is:

| Total | 2 | 3 | 5 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 13 | 14 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.7% | 1.7% | 6.7% | 34% | 17.5% | 17.5% | 17.5% | 4.4% |

- The expected value is about 10.7. The noise traders' fair value should be about the same, though it could be nearer 8.75 if it ignores the trading history.

**Ask.** An ask at 14 or above is almost never bought by an informed trader. It still sells to noise traders who value it about 3 or more above fair. Expected profit per quote:
- Ask 13: about 0.39.
- Ask 14: about 0.50.
- Ask 15–16: about 0.55.

Higher asks pay off less if the noise traders' fair value is really nearer 8.75, so I compromise at 14.5.

**Bid.** A bid of 5 can only lose to an informed trader holding a total of 2 or 3, which is about 2.4% likely. It gains when noise traders value the contract more than about 5.7 below fair. Expected profit is about 0.5 per quote. A bid near 10 has negative expected profit, because informed sellers holding the low totals would cost me more than noise traders pay.

{"bid": 5.0, "ask": 14.5}

Die 2 and die 3 are both revealed as 1, so the settlement value is 2 + die 1. Die 1 is uniform on {0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12}, so the possible values are {2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14}.

**What quote 7 tells us.** Nobody traded at 5 / 14.5.
- An informed trader would have sold at 5 if the value were 2 or 3. No trade makes those values less likely.
- This gives a public fair value of about 10. The low values have probability of about 5% each, and every other value about 15%.

**Choosing the quotes.** I set each side to maximise expected profit against both kinds of trader.
- **Ask:** near 14 to 16, almost no informed buyer can profit, and noise buyers still pay well above 10. An ask of 15 earns about +0.55 per quote.
- **Bid:** near 3 to 4, only the informed seller holding a value of 2 can hurt me. Noise sellers still sell well below 10. A bid of 3.5 earns about +0.46.

My position of +1 allows trading on either side.

{"bid": 3.5, "ask": 15}

With die 2 and die 3 both showing 1, the contract settles at 2 + die 1. Die 1 is uniform over {0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12}, so the settlement value is one of 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, 13 or 14, with a prior mean of 8.75.

**Reading the last two quotes:** Neither quote 7 (5 / 14.5) nor quote 8 (3.5 / 15) traded. An informed trader would have sold at both bids if the value were 2 or 3. So those two values are much less likely now, at roughly 0.13 times the weight of the others. Values 5 and 10–14 each carry about 16% probability. The updated fair value is about 10.5.

**Optimising the last quote:**
- **Ask side:** An ask of 14 or higher means an informed trader never buys. Expected profit is highest at about 15–16, at roughly +0.55.
- **Bid side:** A bid of 5 or lower is only hit by an informed seller if the value is 2 or 3, which is now unlikely. Noise sellers below 5 give an expected profit of about +0.5. Bidding above 5 is worse, because an informed trader holding value 5 starts selling to me.

My position limits allow either side to fill.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 15.5}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 4, 10.
- Die 2 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Expected value of the sum is 12.5:

- **Die 1:** (0 + 1 + 4 + 10) / 4 = 3.75
- **Die 2:** (0 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 9) / 8 = 2.5
- **Die 3:** (0 + 2 + 7 + 7 + 8 + 8 + 9 + 9) / 8 = 6.25

The standard deviation of the sum is about 5.8, close to the noise traders' noise. Half of the counterparties are informed, so I quote a wide spread of about 4 on each side, centred on 12.5. The spread was chosen by judgement, not calculated as the exact optimum.

{"bid": 8.5, "ask": 16.5}

The fair value fell from 12.5 to about 8.9 after the counterparty sold to me at 8.5. I'm quoting around that, skewed slightly lower because I'm long.

**Prior expected value.**
- Die 1 averages 3.75.
- Die 2 averages 2.5.
- Die 3 averages 6.25.
- The total averages 12.5, with a standard deviation of about 5.8.

**What the sale at 8.5 tells me.**
- I enumerated all 256 outcomes. The sum is at most 8 with probability 60/256 = 0.234, and in that case its average is 5.2.
- An informed counterparty sells at 8.5 only if the settlement value is below 8.5.
- A noise trader sells there with probability about 0.245. That is the chance that 12.5 plus noise with standard deviation 5.8 lands below 8.5.
- Weighting the two cases, the updated fair value is (0.5·0.234·5.2 + 0.5·0.245·12.5) / (0.5·0.234 + 0.5·0.245) ≈ 8.9.

**Quote.** I centre the quote near 8.9 and keep a fairly wide spread because half the counterparties are informed. I shade it slightly lower because I'm already long one unit.

{"bid": 5.0, "ask": 12.0}

The prior expected sum is 3.75 + 2.5 + 6.25 = 12.5, with a standard deviation of about 5.8.

The two trades so far roughly cancel out:
- Someone sold to me at 8.5. That price is well below fair, so the seller was more likely informed, which points to a lower value.
- Someone bought from me at 12. That price is close to fair, so it carries a weaker signal.

On balance my fair value is slightly below 12.5, at about 11.5–12. Half of all counterparties are informed, so I keep the spread wide around that centre.

{"bid": 8.0, "ask": 15.5}

The posterior fair value is about 9.6, but it is split into two clusters, so I quote wide: bid 2.6, ask 17.

**Updating the fair value.** Die 1 = 0, so the contract now settles at die 2 + die 3. Before using the trades, that sum has mean 2.5 + 6.25 = 8.75.

The stage-1 trades tell us something. Weighting each trade's informed and noise likelihoods roughly:
- Someone sold at 8.5, which points to a low sum.
- Someone bought at 15.5, which points to a high sum.

The result is two clusters with a gap between them:
- About 54% probability that the sum is 8 or less.
- About 31% probability that the sum is 16–18.

**Choosing the quotes.** I weighed the expected gain from noise traders against the expected loss to informed traders at each price.
- **Ask:** At an ask of 12–13, informed buyers from the high cluster cost more than noise buyers pay. The edge turns positive around 15.5 and is best near 17–17.5, at about +0.3 per quote.
- **Bid:** Any bid near the fair value is drawn down by informed sellers from the low cluster. The edge becomes positive only below about 4.5 and is best around 2.5–3. A buy would also reduce my short position, which is a small plus.

{"bid": 2.6, "ask": 17}

**Quote for step 5: bid 3.6, ask 17.**

1. **What's left to settle.** Die 1 came up 0, so the contract now settles at die 2 + die 3. Before looking at the trades, that has a mean of 2.5 + 6.25 = 8.75. Its range runs from 0 to 18.

2. **What the trades suggest.** I treated each past trade as possibly coming from an informed counterparty and updated on all four quotes. The values were sold at 8.5, bought at 12 and at 15.5, then no trade at 2.6/17.
   - The updated distribution has two clusters. About 52% of the weight is on a sum of 8 or less, mostly 7–8. About 31% is on 16–18.
   - My public fair value comes out around 10.
   - This depends on my rough guesses of how likely noise traders were to trade at each earlier quote.

3. **Choosing the ask.**
   - An ask near 13–15 gets bought mainly by informed traders when the sum is 16–18, which loses money.
   - At 17, noise buyers still pay about 7 above fair value, and only an outcome of 18 hurts me. Expected profit per quote is about +0.37, the best of the levels I checked.

4. **Choosing the bid.**
   - A bid near 8.5 gets hit by informed sellers whenever the sum is 7–8, which loses money.
   - Around 3.5–4, noise sellers still give a good edge and little informed weight sits below the bid. Expected profit per quote is about +0.33.
   - Being short 1, a fill on the bid also reduces my position.

{"bid": 3.6, "ask": 17}

Die 1 = 0, so the settlement value is die 2 plus die 3. The prior expected value is 2.5 + 6.25 = 8.75.

**Updating on stage-2 trading:**
- At quote 4 (2.6 / 17) nobody traded. That makes the extremes of 0–2 and 18 a little less likely.
- At quote 5 someone bought at 17. A noise trader needs about +8 of noise to value the contract above 17, which happens roughly 8% of the time. An informed trader buys only if the value is 18 (die 2 = 9 and die 3 = 9, prior chance 1/32).
- Combining both observations, a value of 18 becomes noticeably more likely. The posterior fair value comes out around 10.6.

**Choosing the quote:**
- **Bid:** If I bid near 6.5, informed traders sell only when the value is 6 or less, where the average value is about 3. Noise traders sell about 24% of the time, with roughly 4 of edge to me. The expected gain is about +0.26.
- **Ask:** At 15.9 or 16.9 I would still be hit by informed buyers when the value is 16–18, and 18 carries heavy posterior weight. An ask of 17.5 is picked off only when the value is 18, and noise buyers still give about 7 of edge. The expected gain is about +0.36.
- **Position:** I am short 2, and selling one more is still within limits.

{"bid": 6.5, "ask": 17.5}

**Settlement**

- Die 1 = 0 and die 3 = 9, so the settlement is 9 + die 2.
- Die 2 is equally likely to be any of 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9. So the settlement is 9, 10, 11, 13 or 18.
- The prior mean is 11.5.

**What stage 2 trading tells us**

- In stage 2 the only way the value could exceed 17 was die 2 = 9 together with die 3 = 9, giving 18.
- At quote 5 someone bought at 17. That is much more likely if the value is 18.
- At quote 4 nobody traded at 2.6 / 17, and at quote 6 nobody traded at 6.5 / 17.5. Both lower the chance of 18, because an informed trader would have bought at those asks.
- I estimated how likely each outcome is under each possible value, assuming each one is equally likely to be an informed or a noise trader. Overall the stage 2 history makes 18 about 2.5 times more likely than the prior says.

**Posterior on the settlement**

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 9 | ~0.32 |
| 10 | ~0.10 |
| 11 | ~0.10 |
| 13 | ~0.21 |
| 18 | ~0.27 |

The expected value is about 12.5.

**Choosing the quotes**

- **Ask:** Anything below 18 gets picked off by an informed buyer whenever the value is 18. An ask of 18 avoids that and still earns about 5.5 on each noise buyer. Its expected profit is about 0.47, the best I found.
- **Bid:** Anything at 9 or above loses to an informed seller when the value is 9. A bid just under 9 avoids that and earns about 3.7 on each noise seller.
- **Position:** I am short 2, so one more sale takes me to -3, which is within the limit. A buy would reduce my risk.

{"bid": 8.8, "ask": 18}

The settlement value is 9 plus die 2. My fair value estimate is about 16.2, well above the naive 11.5, because the trading history points strongly to die 2 = 9.

**Reading the earlier trades** (die 1 = 0 and die 3 = 9 are now known):
- **Quote 5, buy at 17:** an informed trader buys only if the value was above 17. That required die 2 = 9 and die 3 = 9, which is now consistent. A noise trader buys there only about 8% of the time.
- **Quotes 4 and 6, no trade:** these count somewhat against die 2 = 9, because an informed trader would have bought. Taking quotes 4 to 6 together, die 2 = 9 is still about 2.2 times more likely than before.
- **Quotes 2 and 3, buys at 12 and 15.5:** these also favour die 2 = 9 (and die 2 = 4 for quote 2).
- **Quote 1 and quote 7:** these tell us nothing. A sale at 8.5 could not be informed because the value is at least 9. A buy at 18 could not be informed because the value is at most 18.

**Posterior for the settlement value:**

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 18 | about 72% |
| 13 | about 15% |
| 9 to 11 | about 13% |

That gives a fair value of about **16.2**.

**Choosing the quotes:**
- **Ask:** I keep it at 18 or higher so the informed trader never buys. Then I maximise (ask − 16.2) × the chance a noise trader buys. This peaks at about 20.5, with an expected gain of about 0.49.
- **Bid:** I maximise the noise-trader gain minus the expected loss to informed sellers. This peaks at about 10, with an expected gain of about 0.41. Buying here also reduces my short position.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 20.5}

**Settlement value:** die 1 = 0 and die 3 = 9 are known, so the value is 9 plus die 2. That gives possible values of 9, 9, 9, 10, 11, 13, 13 and 18, each equally likely before looking at trades.

- **Quote 2:** the buy at 12 favours 13 or 18.
- **Quote 7:** the buy at 18 must have come from a noise trader, because an informed trader would not pay 18 for a value of at most 18. So it tells us nothing.
- **Quote 8:** no trade at a bid of 10 makes a value of 9 less likely.

Putting these together, I estimate the value is 18 with about 75% probability, and the expected value is roughly 16.5.

**Choosing the quote:**
- **Ask:** I am short 3, and an ask at or below 18 would only be lifted by an informed trader when the value is 18, which loses money. Above 18, only noise traders buy. The expected profit from noise buyers is highest with an ask around 21.
- **Bid:** a bid near 10.5–11 attracts noise sellers. The only cost is an informed trader selling when the value is 9 or 10, which is unlikely given the evidence. I'll use 10.5.

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.
- Die 2 (8 faces, loaded): 1 (prob 1/10), 1 (prob 1/10), 1 (prob 1/10), 7 (prob 1/10), 9 (prob 1/5), 9 (prob 1/5), 11 (prob 1/10), 11 (prob 1/10).
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 1, 3, 3, 3, 5, 6, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
With no dice revealed, the fair value is the sum of the three dice's expected values:

- **Die 1:** mean 6.75, variance 19.44.
- **Die 2:** mean 6.8, variance 15.56.
- **Die 3:** mean 4.875, variance 7.61.

So the fair value is 18.425, with variance about 42.6, giving a standard deviation of about 6.5.

The settlement value's spread (about 6.5) is the same as the noise traders' spread. Treating both as normal, the expected profit on each side is proportional to 2d(1−Φ(z)) − σφ(z), where d is the distance from fair value and z = d/σ. Checking a few values, this peaks around z = 1.2, so d is about 7.8. I'll quote symmetrically around 18.4, though the real dice distribution isn't normal, so this is approximate.

{"bid": 10.6, "ask": 26.2}

Before trading, the expected sum is 6.75 + 6.8 + 4.875 = 18.425. Someone sold to me at 10.6, which is strong evidence the value is low. An informed trader sells only when the sum is 10 or less, which has prior probability of about 0.11. A noise trader sells there with probability of about 0.115.

So after the sale, the low-value case (sum ≤ 10, mean about 6.8) has weight of about 0.49, and the full prior (mean 18.4) has the rest. The posterior fair value is about 12.7.

The value distribution now has two peaks, so informed traders can pick me off on either side. I'll keep a wide spread around 12.7. I'll lean slightly lower because I'm already long one unit.

{"bid": 7.0, "ask": 16.5}

The two sells at my bid suggest the settlement value is low, so I'm marking fair value at about 6.2. I'm quoting wide around that: bid 3.5, ask 13.

**Unconditional expectation**
- Die 1 averages 6.75.
- Die 2 averages 6.8.
- Die 3 averages 4.875.
- The sum averages 18.425.

**Updating on the two sells**
Both counterparties sold to me, at 10.6 and then at 7.
- A noise trader selling below 7 is unlikely, at roughly 7%. The second sell therefore most likely came from an informed trader who knows the value is below 7.
- The prior probabilities of the sum's range are:
  - Below 7 (needs die 2 = 1 and low dice 1 and 3): about 4.7%.
  - From 7 to 10.5: about 6.6%.
  - 10.6 or above: about 88.7%.
- After weighting by how likely each range is to produce these two sells:
  - Below 7 (average about 4.3): about 83%.
  - From 7 to 10.5 (average about 8.5): about 7%.
  - 10.6 or above (average about 19.9): about 10%.
- Fair value is therefore about 6.2.

**Choosing the quotes**
- **Bid:** The sum can never be below 3, so a bid of 3.5 attracts almost no informed sellers. Noise traders sell there about 30% of the time, at roughly 2.7 below fair value.
- **Ask:** An informed buyer only appears if the value is high (about 10%), and then I lose a lot. A wide ask around 13 makes noise-trader sales profitable enough to offset that tail risk. A tighter ask such as 8 has negative expected value.

{"bid": 3.5, "ask": 13}

Fair value is about **5.7**, well below my average entry of 8.8 on the +2 long. I'll post a wide ask at 11.5 and a bid at 4.0.

**Why fair value is about 5.7**
- With die 3 = 3 revealed, the prior expected sum is 6.75 + 6.8 + 3 = 16.55.
- The stage-1 history pulls this down hard. The counterparties sold at 10.6, then sold at 7, then didn't trade inside [3.5, 13].
- Weighting each of those outcomes by whether an informed or a noise trader would produce it gives a posterior on the sum of roughly:
  - 4: about 42% (die 2 = 1, die 1 = 0)
  - 5: about 42% (die 2 = 1, die 1 = 1)
  - 7: about 6%
  - Higher values: about 10% in total, averaging around 14.6.
- The posterior mean is about **5.7**. The noise-trader path I assumed for this is approximate, so the estimate is too.

**Ask**
- The main risk is the informed buyers in the high tail.
- An ask of about 11–12 balances noise-trader buys at roughly fair 5.7 against that tail risk. Expected edge is about +0.35 per quote.

**Bid**
- An informed trader only sells below my bid if the sum is below it, and the sum is almost certainly at least 4.
- So a bid of 4.0 attracts only noise sellers. Expected edge is about +0.3, and I have room to buy one more unit.

{"bid": 4.0, "ask": 11.5}

Given die 3 = 3 and the history, my estimate of the public fair value is about 5.3.

**Prior.** Die 1 averages 6.75 and die 2 averages 6.8, so before any trading the expected sum was about 16.55.

**Updating on the trades.** Counterparties sold to me at 10.6 and then at 7. In quotes 3 and 4 nobody traded inside about 3.5–13. Together these strongly suggest a low total. Most of the probability is on die 2 = 1 with die 1 in {0, 1}, giving a total of 4 or 5. Smaller weights sit on totals of 7, 10, 11 and higher.

**Bid.** The lowest possible total is 4. A bid of 3.9 can never be hit by an informed trader, so it only catches noise sellers at a positive edge. I'm long 2, so I can still buy one more unit.

**Ask.** Above fair value, the ask trades off two effects. Noise buyers pay me the spread over fair value. Informed buyers only buy when the total is high, and then I lose to them.

| Ask | Expected value per quote |
|-----|--------------------------|
| 6 | about −0.08 |
| 8 | about +0.26 |
| 9 | about +0.37 |
| 10 | about +0.43 |

The expected value flattens out around 9–10, so I'll quote 9.5.

{"bid": 3.9, "ask": 9.5}

Posting a wide quote around a fair value of about 4.7: bid 0.5, ask 9.4.

**Fair value.** With die 3 = 3, the starting expectation is 3 + 6.75 (die 1) + 6.8 (die 2) = 16.55. The trading history pulls this down sharply:
- Counterparties sold to me at 10.6 and at 7.
- They then did not trade at 3.5/13, 4/11.5 or 3.9/9.5.

That pattern fits an informed seller who knows the sum is very low. Weighting each possible sum by how well it explains the trades, almost all the probability sits on sums of 4 or 5 (die 1 is 0 or 1 and die 2 shows 1). There is a small weight on 7 and a thin tail above that. The public fair value is about 4.7.

**Bid side.** The lowest possible sum is 0 + 1 + 3 = 4. An informed trader therefore never sells below 4, so any bid at or under 4 is hit only by noise traders. Noise traders value the contract at about 4.7 with a standard deviation of 6.5. Expected profit per quote is roughly the margin times the chance a noise trader sells, and that peaks when the bid is about 0.75 standard deviations (about 4.9) below fair value. I'll bid 0.5.

**Ask side.** Informed buyers only matter if the sum is above my ask, which is very unlikely above about 7. The same margin-versus-hit-rate trade-off points to an ask around 9.4–9.6. That earns about 4.7 from each noise buyer, and informed buyers would only lift it if the sum is 10 or more, which has a tiny probability.

**Position.** I'm long 2, so I have room to buy one more unit and sell up to five.

{"bid": 0.5, "ask": 9.4}

The posterior fair value is about 4.7. I'll quote wide around it: bid 0.5, ask 9.4.

**What is known.** Die 2 = 1 and die 3 = 3, so the settlement is 4 + die 1. Die 1 is one of 0, 1, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11 or 12, so the possible settlements are 4, 5, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16.

**What the history says.** I updated on each quote by asking how likely that outcome was for each value of die 1:
- **Stage 1:** Counterparties sold at 10.6 and then at 7. Informed traders sell there only if the settlement is below those prices, so these trades point strongly to die 1 = 0 or 1.
- **Quotes 3 to 6:** Nobody traded. Informed traders would have bought at the 9.4–11.5 asks if die 1 were 8 or more, so this adds strong evidence that die 1 is small.

**Posterior for die 1.**

| Die 1 | Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4 | about 0.46 |
| 1 | 5 | about 0.46 |
| 3 | 7 | about 0.07 |
| 8 or more | 12 or more | about 0.005 in total |

This gives a fair value of about 4.7.

**Choosing the quote.** Informed traders know the settlement is mostly 4 or 5, so they trade against tight quotes. My edge comes from noise traders, whose valuations spread about 6.5 either side of the fair value.
- **Ask:** At 9.4, informed traders never buy unless die 1 is 8 or more, which has about 0.5% probability. Noise traders buy about 23% of the time, at roughly 4.7 above fair value. Expected value is about +0.5 per quote.
- **Bid:** At 0.5, informed traders never sell, since every possible settlement is above 0.5. Noise traders sell about 25% of the time, at roughly 4 below fair value. Expected value is about +0.5 per quote.

```json
{"bid": 0.5, "ask": 9.4}
```

The quote is **bid 3.9, ask 14**, which is roughly 4 below and 6 above my updated fair value of about 8.

**Fair value**
- Dice 2 and 3 are known and add up to 4. Die 1 is still hidden, so settlement is one of 4, 5, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15 or 16. Each is equally likely before using the trading history.
- At quote 7 (0.5 / 9.4) nobody traded. An informed trader would have bought if the value were 12 or more. So the lack of a trade makes the low outcomes (4, 5, 7) more likely: about 69% low against 31% high.
- That gives a posterior fair value of about 8.0, which is also the centre of the noise traders' valuations.

**Ask side** (I'm long 2, so a sale is welcome)
- The ask needs to be high, so informed buyers only hit it when the outcome is at the very top.
- Expected profit is about +0.43 at an ask of 13.9 and about +0.46 at 14.9.
- I'm choosing about 14.

**Bid side**
- At 3.9 no informed trader can sell to me, because the lowest possible outcome is 4.
- Noise sellers below 3.9 then give an expected profit of about +0.54.
- That beats a bid of 4.9 (about +0.39) or 5.9 (about +0.07).

{"bid": 3.9, "ask": 14}

The contract now settles at 4 plus die 1. I'm long 2, so I want to sell, but only on terms that pay.

**Fair value**
- Die 1 averages 6.75, so with no trading information the settlement value averages 10.75. The possible values are 4, 5, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16.
- Quote 7 (0.5 / 9.4) did not trade. An informed trader would have bought if die 1 were 8 or more. So the no-trade shifts weight towards die 1 being 0, 1 or 3.
- Quote 8 (3.9 / 14) did not trade. An informed trader would have bought if die 1 were 11 or 12. So that no-trade shifts weight away from 15 and 16.
- After both updates, the values 4, 5 and 7 have about 25% probability each. The values 12 to 16 share the remaining 25% or so, with 15 and 16 only a few percent.
- That puts fair value around 7.3. The two sales at my bid in stage 1 also point low.

**Ask**
Expected profit on the sell side is gain from noise buyers minus losses to informed buyers:
- Ask 10: about +0.03, because informed buyers holding values of 12 or more cost almost as much as noise buyers pay.
- Ask 12: about +0.37.
- Ask 14: about +0.47, the best. Only informed traders at 15 or 16 would buy, and they are rare.
- Ask 15: about +0.44.
- Ask 16: about +0.39.

**Bid**
- At a bid of 3.9, no informed trader sells, because the lowest possible value is 4.
- Noise sellers give about +0.5 in expectation.
- So the bid is worth keeping, even though it would add to my long position.
