info.raw:
Before any flips are revealed, the fair value is 4.5 heads. There is a 1/2 chance of the always-heads coin, which gives 6. There is a 1/2 chance of the fair coin, which averages 3. So 0.5·6 + 0.5·3 = 4.5.

The settlement value is lopsided. It is exactly 6 about 50.8% of the time, and otherwise mostly between 2 and 4. I picked each side by estimating expected profit per quote. Gains come from noise traders (65%, valuing at 4.5 ± 1.3) and losses from informed traders (35%, who know the value).

**Ask:**
- At 6.0, an informed trader never buys, because the value can't exceed 6. Noise traders buy about 12% of the time and I earn 1.5 per sale. That gives about **+0.12** per quote.
- At 6.1, I earn more per sale but trade less often, so expected profit drops to about +0.11.
- At 5.5, informed traders holding the 6-head outcome buy often, cutting expected profit to about +0.05.

**Bid:**
- At 3.0, noise traders sell about 12% of the time and I earn 1.5 per purchase. Informed traders sell only when the value is 0–2, which costs about 0.08. Net is about **+0.04**.
- At 3.2 or 3.5, informed traders sell more often, cutting the net to about +0.03 and close to 0.
- At 2.9, the net is about the same as at 3.0 (+0.037).

{"bid": 3.0, "ask": 6.0}

Quoting 3.0 bid and 6.0 ask again maximises expected profit for this quote.

**Fair value.** Before any reveal, the coin is equally likely to be fair or always-heads.
- With the fair coin, heads follow Binomial(6, 0.5), with mean 3.
- With the always-heads coin, the settlement is 6.
- The prior mean is therefore 4.5. P(value = 6) ≈ 0.508.

The no-trade at 3/6 nudges this up slightly, to about 4.55.

**Ask side.** About half the time the true value is 6. Any ask below 6 is hit by informed traders in that case.

| Ask | Noise traders | Informed traders | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.5 | +0.14 | −0.09 | +0.05 |
| 5.9 | | | +0.11 |
| 6.0 | +0.12 | 0 (never adverse) | +0.12, best |
| 6.2 | | | +0.105 |

**Bid side.** The adverse case is the fair coin landing on a low count (0, 1 or 2 heads).

| Bid | Net |
|---|---|
| 3.5 | ≈ 0 |
| 3.1 | +0.033 |
| 3.0 | +0.04, best |
| 2.9 | +0.037 |
| 2.5 | +0.028 |

{"bid": 3.0, "ask": 6.0}

Keeping my quote at 3.0 / 6.0.

**Fair value.** The coin is fair or two-headed with equal odds, so the expected settlement is 0.5 × 3 + 0.5 × 6 = 4.5. The two earlier quotes at 3/6 drew no trades, which tells us little; it nudges fair value slightly above 4.5.

**Ask side.**
- An informed trader buys only if the settlement value is above my ask.
- At an ask of 6, informed traders never buy. Noise traders buy about 12.5% of the time, at about 1.5 above fair value. That is worth about +0.12 per quote.
- An ask of 5.5 attracts more noise buyers. But informed traders buy whenever the value is 6, which is about 51% likely, so that ask is worth only about +0.05.
- So 6 is the better ask.

**Bid side.**
- At a bid of 3, noise sellers are worth about +0.12. Informed sellers cost about −0.08, because they sell when the value is 2 or less. Net is about +0.04.
- A bid of 3.5 nets about 0 and a bid of 2.5 nets about +0.03, so 3 is roughly best.

{"bid": 3.0, "ask": 6.0}

Bid 4.4, ask 6.6. Each side's expected profit is about 0.09–0.14 per quote.

**Fair value after two heads.**

- So the chance the coin is fair is now 0.125 / 0.625 = 0.2, and the chance it is two-headed is 0.8.

- Fair value = 0.8 × 6 + 0.2 × 4 = 5.6.
- The no-trade history at 3/6 adds almost no information, so I keep 5.6.

**Settlement distribution.**

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 6 | 0.8125 |
| 5 | 0.05 |
| 4 | 0.075 |
| 3 | 0.05 |
| 2 | 0.0125 |

**Ask.** For each candidate ask I added the expected cost of selling to an informed trader and the expected gain from noise traders.
- Settlement can never exceed 6, so an ask of 6.0 or higher is never hit by an informed trader. Any sale there is a guaranteed gain.
- Expected profit by ask: 6.0 gives 0.099, 6.2 gives 0.126, 6.4 gives 0.140, 6.6 gives 0.144 (the peak), and 6.8 gives 0.139.

**Bid.** Same method on the buy side.
- An informed trader sells to me only when settlement is below my bid, which costs me.
- Expected profit by bid: 5.0 gives 0.051, 4.8 gives 0.075, 4.6 gives 0.089, 4.4 gives 0.094 (the peak), and 4.2 gives 0.092.

{"bid": 4.4, "ask": 6.6}

- The rest comes from the fair coin: P(5) = 0.05, P(4) = 0.075, P(3) = 0.05, P(2) = 0.0125.

**Update from the no-trade at quote 4 (4.4 / 6.6).**
- An informed trader knowing a value of 2, 3 or 4 would have sold at 4.4, so no trade makes those values less likely.

- If it's the always-heads coin, the contract settles at 6.
- If it's the fair coin, the number of heads is binomial(6, 0.5), with mean 3.
- So the expected settlement value is 0.5 × 3 + 0.5 × 6 = 4.5.
- The chance it settles at exactly 6 is about 0.51 (1/2 + 1/128).
- Otherwise it lands between 0 and 5, in proportions 1:6:15:20:15:6.

**Ask side**
- Informed traders buy whenever the true value is 6, which happens about half the time.
- Any ask below 6 loses to them in those cases.
- An ask of 6.0 never loses to an informed buyer.
- It still sells to noise traders about 12% of the time, at a profit of 1.5 over fair value.
- That gives an expected profit of about +0.12 per quote, roughly the best of the asks I checked.

**Bid side**
- Informed traders sell whenever the true value is below the bid.
- A bid of 3.0 gains about 0.12 from noise traders and loses about 0.08 to informed sellers.
- That nets about +0.04, the best of the bids I checked.
- A bid of 3.5 nets roughly zero, and 2.5 nets about +0.03.

**Update from quote 1.** The counterparty sold at 3.
- An informed trader sells only if the value is 0, 1 or 2. The prior chance of that is 22/128, about 0.17.
- A noise trader sells if its valuation is below 3, which has probability Φ(−1.5/1.3), about 0.12.
- After this update, the fair value is about 3.27.

**Ask.** The main risk is selling to an informed trader when the value is 6.
- At 4, the expected loss to informed buyers is larger than the expected gain from noise buyers.
- At 5.5, the expected gain is slightly positive.
- Selling also reduces my long position, which is a bonus.

**Bid.**
- At 2.5, expected profit is about −0.02.
- At 2.0, expected profit is about +0.07, the best of the levels checked.
- At 1.5, expected profit is about +0.06.

|-----|-----------------|
| 1.5 | +0.04 |
| 1.1 | +0.09 |
| 1.0 | +0.10 |
| 0.9 | +0.10 |

A bid of 1.0 is about the best, and buying one more unit would only take me to +3, inside the limit of +4.

info.raw:
The expected settlement value is about 48.8: the chance of heads averages 0.4×0.3 + 0.1×0.4 + 0.5×0.9 = 0.61, and 8 flips × 10 × 0.61 = 48.8.

The value is split in two. A low-bias coin settles near 24–32. A high-bias coin settles near 72. So an informed trader's value is usually about 24 away from 48.8, and a tight spread would lose to them.

I compared half-spreads by trading the gain from noise traders (whose valuations have SD 26) against the loss to informed traders. A half-spread of about 25 gave the best expected edge, around 5 per quote. That puts the quote at roughly 24–73, which sits just outside both clusters.

{"bid": 24, "ask": 73}

The prior expected value is 80 × 0.61 ≈ 48.8. The counterparty sold at 24, which shifts the estimate down. A trader with full information sells there only if 3 or fewer heads, or equivalently a settlement value of 20 or less.

**Updating on the sale**
- Any counterparty sells at 24 with probability 0.4605 if there are 2 or fewer heads. Otherwise the probability is 0.1105, which comes only from noise traders.
- The new public fair value is about 33.6.
- The outcome is strongly two-peaked:
  - About 58% weight on 0–2 heads, mostly 1–2 heads.
  - About 27% weight on 6–8 heads.

**Fair value**

**Trading history**

Settlement is 30 plus 10 times the remaining heads:

| Settlement | 70 | 60 | 50 | 40 | 30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.50 | 0.25 | 0.11 | 0.10 | 0.05 |

**Ask**

**Bid**

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 70 | 0.50 |
| 60 | 0.25 |
| 50 | 0.11 |
| 40 | 0.10 |
| 30 | 0.05 |

| 0.9 | 0.958 |

info.raw:
Quote: bid 21, ask 75.

**Fair value.** The expected chance of heads is 0.4·0.3 + 0.1·0.4 + 0.5·0.9 = 0.61. Over 8 flips at 10 per head, the expected settlement is 48.8.

**Shape of the settlement.** The outcome is split in two clusters. If a low-bias coin was picked, settlement is likely around 20–30. If the 0.9 coin was picked, it is likely 70–80.

**Ask side.** The informed trader mostly buys when the 0.9 coin was picked.
- I estimated expected profit per quote as noise-trader profit minus informed-trader loss.
- At an ask of about 74–76, the loss to informed buyers is small.
- Noise traders still buy often enough to earn about 2.3 per quote.

**Bid side.** The informed trader mostly sells when a low-bias coin was picked.
- With a bid around 20–21, the loss to informed sellers stays moderate.
- Noise-trader profit makes the expected gain about 2.0 per quote.

{"bid": 21, "ask": 75}

Before any trade, the expected heads per flip is 0.4·0.3 + 0.1·0.4 + 0.5·0.9 = 0.61, so the fair value is about 48.8. The settlement value has two clusters: around 20–30 if the coin is a low-heads coin, and around 70–80 if it is the 0.9 coin.

**What the quote-1 no-trade tells us.** An informed counterparty would have traded unless the head count was between 3 and 7. A noise trader would have declined about 70% of the time. Updating on that moves the fair value slightly, to about 50.

**Choosing the quotes.**
- **Ask at 70:** an informed counterparty buys only when the count is 8, losing me about 10. Noise traders buy about 22% of the time for a gain of about 20. Net expected value is clearly positive.
- **Bid at 30:** an informed counterparty sells when the count is 2 or fewer (roughly 20–25% chance), costing me about 16 on average. Noise traders sell about 22% of the time for a gain of about 20. Net expected value is also positive.

{"bid": 30, "ask": 70}

Fair value given flips 1,0,0,0 is about **22.9**. I'm quoting bid 5 and ask 44.

**Posterior on the coin.** For each coin, the chance of seeing 1 head and 3 tails, times its prior:
- P(heads) = 0.3: 0.3 × 0.7³ = 0.1029, times 0.4 = 0.04116.
- P(heads) = 0.4: 0.4 × 0.6³ = 0.0864, times 0.1 = 0.00864.
- P(heads) = 0.9: 0.9 × 0.1³ = 0.0009, times 0.5 = 0.00045.

Normalising gives posterior weights of about 0.819, 0.172 and 0.009.

**Fair value.**
- The expected chance of heads is now about 0.323.
- That gives about 1.29 expected heads in the 4 remaining flips.
- Fair value is 10 + 12.9 ≈ 22.9.

**Settlement range.** Settlement can only be 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50. The approximate chances are 0.23, 0.41, 0.27, 0.08 and 0.01. These assume the coin is the 0.3 one, which is about 82% likely.

**Bid.**
- Settlement can never be below 10, so a bid at 10 or less is never hit by an informed trader.
- Lowering the bid further widens the edge on noise traders but makes them trade less often.
- Expected profit per quote is about 2.6 at a bid of 10 and 2.9 at a bid of 5. It falls slightly below that at a bid of 0.
- So I bid 5.

**Ask.**
- At an ask near 30, informed buyers cost a lot when settlement is 40 or 50.
- Expected profit per quote is about 2.8 at an ask of 39 and about 2.85 at 45. Informed losses are close to zero at both.
- So I ask 44.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 44}

Posterior after the four revealed flips (1 head, 3 tails):
- **Coin with P(heads) = 0.3:** about 0.819
- **Coin with P(heads) = 0.4:** about 0.172
- **Coin with P(heads) = 0.9:** about 0.009

So the expected P(heads) for each remaining flip is about 0.323.

Fair value = 10 (one head so far) + 4 × 10 × 0.323 ≈ **22.9**.

The settlement value can only be 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50.
- **Bid at or below 9:** an informed counterparty never sells to me, since the value is at least 10. Bids around 3–5 maximise the expected edge from noise traders.
- **Ask:** an ask of about 41–45 is only hit by an informed counterparty when the value is 50, which has a probability of about 1.7%. Expected profit is highest in that range.

{"bid": 5, "ask": 42}

Expected settlement is about 26.4, which puts my bid at 8 and my ask at 46.

**Coin posterior after 6 flips (2 heads, 4 tails).** I weight each prior by the likelihood of 2 heads and 4 tails:

| P(heads) | Prior × likelihood | Posterior |
|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 0.4 × 0.021609 = 0.008644 | 0.8035 |
| 0.4 | 0.1 × 0.020736 = 0.002074 | 0.1928 |
| 0.9 | 0.5 × 0.000081 = 0.0000405 | 0.0038 |

This gives E[p] ≈ 0.3216.

**Settlement distribution.** The 2 heads so far are worth 20, and flips 7 and 8 are still to come.

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 20 (no more heads) | 0.463 |
| 30 (one more head) | 0.431 |
| 40 (two more heads) | 0.106 |

The fair value is about 26.4.

**The earlier buy at 42 tells me nothing.** For an informed trader to buy at 42, the contract would have had to settle at 50 or more. That needed flips 5 to 8 all to be heads, but flips 5 and 6 include a tail. So that buyer was a noise trader, and I make no update.

**Choosing the ask.** I compare noise profit against losses to informed buyers:
- An ask of 31 nets about 0.96.
- An ask of 39 nets about 2.54.
- An ask of 40 or more nets about 2.65, because informed buyers stop trading there.
- The ask peaks at around 45 to 47, netting about 2.87.

**Choosing the bid.** With the bid at 20 or below, informed sellers never trade with me. Noise profit flattens out between bids of 8 and 10, at about 2.86.

{"bid": 8, "ask": 46}

This is the last quote, so I only need the bid and ask that maximise expected profit on this one trade. My short position of 1 doesn't change that choice.

**Probability of each coin**, given the 6 revealed flips (2 heads, 4 tails):

| Coin P(heads) | Prior | Likelihood × prior | Probability now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 2/5 | 0.3² × 0.7⁴ × 0.4 ≈ 0.00864 | ≈ 0.804 |
| 0.4 | 1/10 | 0.4² × 0.6⁴ × 0.1 ≈ 0.00207 | ≈ 0.193 |
| 0.9 | 1/2 | 0.9² × 0.1⁴ × 0.5 ≈ 0.00004 | ≈ 0.004 |

- The expected heads probability of the coin is about 0.32.
- Fair value = 10 × (2 + 2 × 0.32) ≈ 26.4.

**Settlement distribution.** Flips 7 and 8 are still unknown:
- Settles at 20 with probability ≈ 0.46.
- Settles at 30 with probability ≈ 0.43.
- Settles at 40 with probability ≈ 0.11.

**Ask.**
- At 40 or above, an informed trader never buys, since the value is at most 40.
- Noise traders value the contract at 26.4 plus noise with standard deviation 26.
- Expected noise profit is (a − 26.4) × P(noise value > a). This peaks near a ≈ 46, at about 4.4 × 0.65 ≈ 2.9 per quote.
- Asks between 30 and 40 earn less from noise traders and also lose to informed buyers when the value is 40.

**Bid.**
- At 20 or below, an informed trader never sells, since the value is at least 20.
- Expected noise profit is (26.4 − b) × P(noise value < b). This peaks near b ≈ 7, at about 2.9 per quote.
- Bids above 20 lose heavily to informed sellers when the value is 20, which happens 46% of the time.

{"bid": 7, "ask": 46}

{"bid": 18.8, "ask": 30.8}

Fair value before any reveal: E[P(heads)] = 0.6·0.5 + 0.4·0.8 = 0.62, so expected heads = 8 × 0.62 = 4.96 and fair ≈ 24.8. The settlement can only be a multiple of 5, with a standard deviation of about 8.8.

Before any flips are revealed, the chance of heads is 0.6×0.5 + 0.4×0.8 = 0.62. That gives 4.96 expected heads, so fair value is 24.8. The standard deviation of the settlement is about 8.8. {"bid": 20.4, "ask": 28.4}

{"bid": 22.5, "ask": 28.5}

The settlement value is either 20 or 25, with expected value about 22.83, so I'm quoting a bid of 18.0 and an ask of 27.8.

I ignored any information carried by the earlier trades, since its effect is minor now that seven flips are known.

|---|---|

| 27 | 0.88 |
| 28 | 0.90 |
| 29 | 0.87 |

**Fair value**

- Expected value = 20 + 5 × 0.566 ≈ 22.83.

**Ask**
- An ask at 25 or higher can never be lifted by an informed trader, because the most the contract can be worth is 25.

**Bid**

**Position**
My position limits don't constrain this choice.

{"bid": 17.6, "ask": 28.0}

- The revealed flips show 4 heads in 7.

- Weighting by the priors (0.6 and 0.4) gives P(biased coin) ≈ 0.2185.

- Expected profit on the bid side is P(valuation < bid) × (22.83 − bid). This peaks around a bid of 18, at about 1.12.

My position is −1, so either trade keeps me within the ±3 limit.

- Fair value ≈ 2 heads already + 4 × 0.557 ≈ 4.23.

**Ask at 5.0:** An informed buyer only trades if the settlement is 6, which needs all four remaining flips to be heads (probability about 13%). I still capture noise buyers with about 0.77 of edge.

**Bid at 3.0:** An informed seller only trades if the settlement is 2, which needs no more heads (probability about 7%). I still capture noise sellers with about 1.23 of edge.

My position of -1 leaves room on both sides.

{"bid": 3.0, "ask": 5.0}

**Fair value estimate.** The revealed flips so far are 1, 1, 0.

Each coin's chance of producing those flips is p²(1−p). Multiplying by the prior gives:
- p = 0.2: 0.0096
- p = 0.5: 0.05
- p = 0.7: 0.0441

Normalising, the posterior is about 0.093, 0.482 and 0.425. That gives E[p] ≈ 0.557.

Four flips are still unrevealed, so expected settlement is 2 + 4 × 0.557 ≈ 4.23.

**Adjusting for the last trade.** At quote 8 someone bought at 5. Only an informed trader expecting 6 or more heads would buy there for sure. That needs all 4 remaining flips to be heads, which has a chance of about 13%. This trade tilts the estimate a little upward, to roughly 4.35.

**Inventory.** I am short 2, so I want to buy back. I'll skew my quotes slightly upward and keep the spread wide enough to cover the risk of trading with an informed counterparty.

{"bid": 3.8, "ask": 5.2}

Settlement is 3 already-revealed heads plus heads from flips 6 and 7. After 3 heads in 5 flips, the posterior on the coin is:

| P(heads) | Posterior |
|---|---|
| 0.2 | ≈ 0.066 |
| 0.5 | ≈ 0.537 |
| 0.7 | ≈ 0.398 |

- The expected heads probability is about 0.56, so fair value ≈ 3 + 2(0.56) ≈ 4.12.
- The settlement can only be 3, 4 or 5. Their probabilities are about 0.21, 0.46 and 0.33.

**Ask side:**
- An informed trader buys only if the value is 5 and my ask is below 5.
- If my ask is above 5, informed traders never hurt me on this side.

**Bid side:**
- An informed trader sells only if the value is 3 and my bid is above 3.
- If my bid is below 3, informed traders never hurt me on this side either.

**Noise traders** (sd 2.7): expected edge is x·Φ(−x/2.7), where x is my distance from fair value. This is largest near x ≈ 2–2.5, giving about 0.44–0.46 per quote. Quoting about 2 away on each side earns that and avoids losses to informed traders.

I'm short 2, so I skew slightly toward buying back, while staying wide.

{"bid": 2.2, "ask": 6.0}

Using Bayes on the 5 revealed flips (3 heads, 2 tails), the probability of each coin is about 0.066 for P(heads)=0.2, 0.537 for 0.5, and 0.398 for 0.7. That gives an expected heads rate of about 0.56 on each remaining flip.

Two flips are left, so settlement can only be 3, 4 or 5, with probabilities of about 0.21, 0.46 and 0.33. The fair value is about 3 + 1.12 = 4.12.

**Informed traders:** settlement is a whole number and they trade only on strict inequality. With a bid at or below 3 and an ask at or above 5, they never trade against me.

**Noise traders:** their valuations have a spread of 2.7. Expected profit per quote is roughly 0.8 × distance from fair × chance the trader crosses my price. This is largest when each side sits about 1.65 from fair value.

That puts the bid near 2.5 and the ask near 5.8. Both are outside the range where informed traders would act.

{"bid": 2.5, "ask": 5.8}

Bid 2.1, no ask (position is −3, so the ask is pulled).

**Fair value is about 4.12.**
- The revealed flips show 3 heads and 2 tails.
- Updating the coin's bias on those flips gives these posterior probabilities:

| P(heads) | Posterior probability |
|---|---|
| 0.2 | ≈ 0.066 |
| 0.5 | ≈ 0.537 |
| 0.7 | ≈ 0.397 |

- That makes E[P(heads)] ≈ 0.56, so flips 6 and 7 should add about 1.12 heads.
- Expected settlement is 3 + 1.12 ≈ 4.12.
- The buy at 5.8 last quote must have come from a noise trader, because settlement can be at most 5. So the trading history doesn't shift this estimate.

**Informed traders:** with any bid below 3, an informed counterparty never sells to me, since settlement is at least 3. So below 3 I face no adverse selection.

**Noise traders:** a noise trader sells if their valuation, drawn from N(4.12, 2.7), is below my bid. Expected profit is 0.8 × P(sell) × (4.12 − bid):

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 3.0 | ≈ 0.30 |
| 2.5 | ≈ 0.355 |
| 2.0 to 2.1 | ≈ 0.367 (the peak) |

{"bid": 2.1, "ask": null}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.3 with probability 1/5, P(heads) = 0.4 with probability 3/10, P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
The coin's expected P(heads) is 0.43, so the expected settlement is 6 × 0.43 = 2.58. The standard deviation of the settlement is about 1.29.

Because the settlement is a whole number of heads, informed traders only act when the true count is above my ask or below my bid. Integer quotes are best: at a price of exactly 4, a buyer whose value is 4 does not trade.

**Ask side** (expected profit per quote):

| Ask | Loss to informed | Gain from noise | Net |
|-----|------------------|-----------------|-----|
| 3.7 | −0.075 | +0.109 | +0.034 |
| 3.9 | −0.051 | +0.102 | +0.052 |
| 4.0 | −0.039 | +0.098 | **+0.058** |
| 4.2 | −0.032 | +0.086 | +0.054 |

**Bid side** (expected profit per quote):

| Bid | Loss to informed | Gain from noise | Net |
|-----|------------------|-----------------|-----|
| 2.0 | −0.127 | +0.095 | −0.032 |
| 1.1 | −0.033 | +0.095 | +0.062 |
| 1.0 | −0.023 | +0.089 | **+0.066** |
| 0.9 | −0.020 | +0.083 | +0.063 |

The best quote is a bid of 1.0 and an ask of 4.0.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.0}

A buy at my ask of 4 is fairly strong evidence of 5 or more heads. That buy means one of two things:
- The buyer was informed and the true count is 5 or 6.
- The buyer was a noise trader with an unusually high valuation.

**Updating the fair value**
- Before any trades, the expected chance of heads is 0.2×0.3 + 0.3×0.4 + 0.5×0.5 = 0.43. That gives an expected count of 2.58 heads.
- Before trading, P(5 or 6 heads) ≈ 0.069.
- A noise trader buys above 4 with probability ≈ 0.138 (needs noise above 1.42, with SD 1.3).
- After the buy, P(5 or 6 heads) ≈ 0.38 and the public fair value is ≈ 3.43.
- The updated chances by count are: 6 heads ≈ 0.05, 5 heads ≈ 0.33, 4 heads ≈ 0.11, and 3 or fewer ≈ 0.51.

**Choosing the ask**
- An ask of 5.0 means an informed buyer only takes it if the count is 6.
- A noise trader still buys about 11% of the time, and I gain about 1.57 per unit when they do.
- Expected profit is about +0.06, which beats asks of 4.5 (≈ -0.01) and 4.9 (≈ +0.05).

**Choosing the bid**
- A bid near 3 loses heavily to informed sellers, because there is a large chance of 3 or fewer heads.
- A bid around 1.0 gives the best expected profit, about +0.02.
- A bid of 2.0 gives about +0.01, and 1.5 about +0.02.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 5.0}

Fair value after flip 1 = 0 and the two earlier trades is about 1.4, though this estimate is rough.

**Flip 1 alone.** A tail makes the low-bias coins more likely. The posterior bias is 0.3 with probability 0.246, 0.4 with 0.316, and 0.5 with 0.439. That gives expected P(heads) of about 0.419. With 5 flips left, the expected settlement is about 2.10.

**The two earlier trades.**
- Someone bought at 4. If they were informed, the settlement is 5 or more.
- Someone sold at 1. If they were informed, the settlement is 0.
- Both cannot be informed, so at least one was a noise trader.
- Weighting each possible settlement by how likely it makes this pair of trades raises P(settlement = 0) to about 50%. P(settlement = 5) becomes about 7%.
- That pulls the public fair value down to roughly 1.3–1.5.

**Bid at 0.2.**
- An informed seller only hits it when the settlement is 0, which costs at most 0.2.
- Noise traders sell below 0.2 often enough to make the bid slightly profitable.

**Ask at 3.1.**
- Informed buyers only lift it when the settlement is 4 or 5, which is fairly unlikely now.
- Noise traders who pay 3.1 against a fair value near 1.4 give a positive edge.

{"bid": 0.2, "ask": 3.1}

After flip 1 came up tails, the fair value is about 2.1 heads. The sell at 0.2 on quote 3 then pulls it down to about 1.0.

**Before the last trade.** Flip 1 = 0 (tails) updates the coin probabilities:
- P(heads) = 0.3: 0.246
- P(heads) = 0.4: 0.316
- P(heads) = 0.5: 0.439

That gives E[p] ≈ 0.419. Five flips remain, so the expected settlement is about 5 × 0.419 ≈ 2.10.

**What the sell at 0.2 tells us.**
- An informed trader only sells at 0.2 if the settlement is 0.
- Before the trade, P(settlement = 0) ≈ 0.08.
- If the settlement is 0, the chance of that sell was about 0.5 + 0.5 × 0.07 ≈ 0.54.
- Otherwise it was about 0.5 × 0.07 ≈ 0.036, from noise traders alone.
- Updating, P(settlement = 0) ≈ 0.56.
- If the settlement is above 0, its expected value is about 2.28.
- So the public fair value is now about 0.44 × 2.28 ≈ 1.0.

**Ask.** Selling to informed traders loses money when the settlement is above the ask. Noise traders pay (ask − 1.0) when they buy.
- Ask 2.5: net expected profit ≈ +0.03.
- Ask 3.0: net expected profit ≈ +0.035, the best of the three.
- Ask 3.5: net expected profit ≈ +0.02.

**Bid.** At a bid of 0, informed traders never sell, because the settlement cannot be below 0. Noise traders sell when their valuation is below 0, which happens about 22% of the time. Each such purchase gains about 1.0, for an expected profit of about +0.11. Any bid above 0 would buy from every informed trader when the settlement is 0, which is a likely outcome.

My position is +1, so neither trade would breach the ±4 limit.

{"bid": 0.0, "ask": 3.0}

**Fair value**

After five tails in a row, the posterior on each coin is proportional to its prior times the chance of five tails:

| Coin P(heads) | Prior × P(5 tails) | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 0.2 × 0.7⁵ | 0.0336 |
| 0.4 | 0.3 × 0.6⁵ | 0.0233 |
| 0.5 | 0.5 × 0.5⁵ | 0.0156 |

So P(flip 6 = heads) = (0.0336·0.3 + 0.0233·0.4 + 0.0156·0.5) / 0.0726 ≈ **0.375**.

The contract settles at either 0 or 1, and its fair value is about 0.375.

**Ask side**
- Any ask of 1 or higher can never be lifted by an informed trader, because the most the contract can be worth is 1. Only noise traders, whose valuation is 0.375 plus noise with standard deviation 1.3, will buy.
- Expected profit per quote is then 0.5 × P(noise > x) × x, where x is my ask minus 0.375. This is highest at about x ≈ 1, which gives an ask of about **1.4**.
- At x = 1, the expected profit is about 0.5 × 0.22 × 1 ≈ 0.11.
- Asks below 1 do worse once losses to informed buyers are counted. For example, an ask of 0.9 earns about 0.07.

**Bid side**
- Any bid of 0 or lower can never be hit by an informed trader, because the contract is worth at least 0. Only noise traders will sell.
- The same calculation applies in reverse. The best bid is about 0.375 − 1 ≈ **−0.6**, with expected profit of about 0.11.
- A bid of exactly 0 would earn only about 0.07.
- Any positive bid loses money to informed sellers when flip 6 is tails, which happens with probability 0.625.

Buying would take my position from +1 to +2, which is well within the limit of +4.

{"bid": -0.6, "ask": 1.4}

Five tails have now been revealed, so the contract settles at either 0 or 1, depending only on flip 6.

**Posterior on the coin after 5 tails**

| P(heads) | Prior × likelihood | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 0.2 × 0.7⁵ | 0.0336 |
| 0.4 | 0.3 × 0.6⁵ | 0.0233 |
| 0.5 | 0.5 × 0.5⁵ | 0.0156 |

So the chance that flip 6 is heads, and therefore the fair value, is about **0.375**.

**Why quote outside 0 to 1**
- An informed trader values the contract at exactly 0 or 1.
- If my ask is 1 or higher, no informed trader buys. If my bid is 0 or lower, no informed trader sells.
- Only noise traders can then trade with me. Their valuation is 0.375 plus noise with standard deviation 1.3.
- For each side, expected profit = 0.5 × P(noise trader reaches my quote) × (distance of my quote from fair value).

**Choosing the ask**

| Ask | P(noise trader buys) | Edge over 0.375 | Product |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.3 | 0.238 | 0.925 | 0.220 |
| 1.4 | 0.215 | 1.025 | 0.221 |
| 1.5 | 0.194 | 1.125 | 0.218 |

The best ask is about 1.4.

**Choosing the bid**
By symmetry the best bid is about 0.375 − 1.0, which is −0.6 or −0.7. At a bid of −0.6, a noise trader sells with probability about 0.227 and my edge is 0.975, giving a product of about 0.221.

Being long 1 unit does not change the quote, because the objective is expected profit, not risk.

{"bid": -0.6, "ask": 1.4}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.3 with probability 1/5, P(heads) = 0.4 with probability 3/10, P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 1/2. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
The prior expected number of heads is 6 × 0.43 = 2.58, with a standard deviation of about 1.29. For each quote level I weighed the expected loss to informed traders against the expected gain from noise traders. The best levels are a bid of about 1.0 and an ask of about 4.0. At those prices each side has a small positive edge of roughly +0.06.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.0}

Quoting **bid 1.0 / ask 4.0**, the same as quote 1: each side is profitable on its own, and narrower quotes lose more to informed traders than they gain from noise traders.

**Fair value.** The expected chance of heads is 0.2·0.3 + 0.3·0.4 + 0.5·0.5 = 0.43. So expected heads over 6 flips is about 2.58. The lack of a trade at 1/4 barely changes this.

**Settlement distribution (mixture of the three coins):**

| Heads | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.045 | 0.163 | 0.275 | 0.276 | 0.171 | 0.060 | 0.009 |

**Choosing each side.** Settlement is always a whole number, so a bid exactly at 1.0 is hit by an informed trader only when the value is 0. An ask exactly at 4.0 is lifted by an informed trader only when the value is 5 or 6.

- **Bid 1.0:**
  - The informed seller costs about 0.045.
  - Noise traders earn about 0.112 × 1.58 ≈ 0.177.
  - Net is about +0.066 per arrival, the best of the bids I checked.
  - Bid 1.2 nets about +0.056, bid 1.5 about +0.035, and bid 2.0 loses money.
- **Ask 4.0:**
  - The informed buyer costs about 0.078.
  - Noise traders earn about 0.196.
  - Net is about +0.059 per arrival.
  - Ask 3.5 nets only about +0.01, and ask 3.0 loses money.

{"bid": 1.0, "ask": 4.0}

Fair value is about 3.22, so I'm quoting wide around it: bid 1.9, ask 4.8. Both sides should earn roughly +0.06 to +0.07 per quote in expectation.

**Fair value**
- Seeing a head on flip 1 shifts the coin probabilities from 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5 to about 0.14 / 0.28 / 0.58 for P(heads) = 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.5.
- That makes the expected chance of heads about 0.444.
- Fair value is 1 (flip 1) + 5 × 0.444 ≈ 3.22.

**Ask side**
- At any ask between 4 and 5, an informed trader only buys when the settlement is 5 or more. That happens about 14% of the time.
- An ask of 4.8 limits that loss. A noise trader still crosses it often enough to give an edge of about +0.06.

**Bid side**
- With a bid just under 2, an informed trader only sells when the settlement is 1. That happens about 6% of the time.
- A noise trader crosses 1.9 about 15% of the time, giving an edge of about +0.07.
- A higher bid such as 2.9 would let informed traders sell at a settlement of 2, which loses money overall.

{"bid": 1.9, "ask": 4.8}

Expected settlement after flip 1 = 1 is about 3.22, and my quotes of 1.9 / 4.9 each have small positive expected value.

**Posterior on the coin given flip 1 = 1**
- The unnormalised weights are 0.2×0.3 = 0.06, 0.3×0.4 = 0.12 and 0.5×0.5 = 0.25, which sum to 0.43.
- Normalised, the posterior is 0.140 (for 0.3), 0.279 (for 0.4) and 0.581 (for 0.5).
- The expected heads probability is 0.444.
- So the public fair value is 1 + 5 × 0.444 ≈ 3.22.

**Settlement distribution**
Settlement S equals 1 plus the number of heads in flips 2–6:

| S | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P(S) | 0.063 | 0.213 | 0.321 | 0.264 | 0.116 | 0.021 |

Settlement is always a whole number, so quoting just inside an integer avoids trading with informed counterparties at that integer.

**Ask side**
- An ask of 3.9 earns about 0.003 per quote.
- An ask of 4.5 earns about 0.059.
- An ask of 4.9 earns about 0.065, and 4.7 is close at about 0.063.
- At 4.9, an informed buyer only takes it when S is 5 or 6.

**Bid side**
- A bid of 2.9 has negative expected value, because informed sellers hit it whenever S is 1 or 2.
- A bid of 1.9 earns about 0.074. Only S = 1 informed sellers hit it, which happens with probability 0.063, while noise sellers hit it about 15% of the time.

{"bid": 1.9, "ask": 4.9}

Five flips are revealed with 2 heads, so the contract will settle at either 2 or 3 depending on flip 6.

**Updating the coin's bias on 2 heads in 5 flips**
- Weights (prior × likelihood): p=0.3 gives 0.2 × 0.03087 = 0.00617; p=0.4 gives 0.3 × 0.03456 = 0.01037; p=0.5 gives 0.5 × 0.03125 = 0.01563.
- Normalised posterior: 0.19, 0.32, 0.49, so the expected P(heads) is about 0.429.
- Fair value is 2 + 0.429 = **2.43**. Settlement is 2 with probability about 0.57 and 3 with about 0.43.

**Quoting**
- **Bid:** keep it at or below 2. An informed trader whose value is 2 then never sells, so only noise traders sell to me.
  - Expected profit from my bid side is 0.5 × P(noise sells) × (2.43 − bid).
  - This peaks around a bid of 1.4–1.5, at about 0.11.
- **Ask:** keep it at or above 3. An informed trader whose value is 3 then never buys, so only noise traders buy from me.
  - Expected profit from my ask side is 0.5 × P(noise buys) × (ask − 2.43).
  - This peaks around an ask of 3.4–3.5, at about 0.11.

{"bid": 1.4, "ask": 3.4}

Five flips are revealed and they show 2 heads, so the contract settles at 2 + flip 6. The settlement can only be 2 or 3.

**Which coin is it?** I weighted each coin by its prior times the chance of seeing 2 heads in 5 flips:
- p = 0.3: 0.2 × 0.3² × 0.7³ ≈ 0.00617
- p = 0.4: 0.3 × 0.4² × 0.6³ ≈ 0.01037
- p = 0.5: 0.5 × 0.5² × 0.5³ ≈ 0.01563

This gives an expected heads probability for flip 6 of about 0.429. The fair value is therefore about **2.43**.

**Informed traders.** They value the contract at exactly 2 or 3.
- With a bid at or below 2, they never sell to me.
- With an ask at or above 3, they never buy from me.
- So keeping my quotes outside the range 2 to 3 means informed traders never trade with me.

**Noise traders.** Their valuation is 2.43 plus noise with standard deviation 1.3. On each side, my expected profit is 0.5 × (my edge over 2.43) × (chance they trade).
- Bid side: this is about 0.110 at a bid of 1.4, close to the peak. A bid of 1.8 gives about 0.099.
- Ask side: this is about 0.11 at an ask of 3.4 or 3.5, close to the peak. An ask of 3.0 gives about 0.094.

So I quote a bid of 1.4 and an ask of 3.4.

{"bid": 1.4, "ask": 3.4}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 2/5, P(heads) = 0.7 with probability 3/5. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 7 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Before any reveals, the fair value is about 43.4.

**Fair value**
- The expected chance of heads is 0.4 × 0.5 + 0.6 × 0.7 = 0.62.
- Over 7 flips that gives 7 × 0.62 = 4.34 expected heads, so the contract is worth about 43.4.
- The settlement value has a standard deviation of about 14.3. That is more than the noise traders' spread of 11, so informed traders have a large edge.

**Choosing the spread**
I compared expected profit per quote for different half-spreads around 43.4. Noise traders earn me the spread when they trade. Informed traders cost me whenever the settlement value lands outside my quotes.

| Half-spread | Net profit per quote |
|---|---|
| 8 | about 0.57 |
| 10 | about 0.85 |
| 12 | about 0.99 |
| 13.4 | about 1.02 |

A wide spread does best. I set the bid at 30.0, just above the 3-heads value of 30, so I don't buy from informed sellers who know only 3 heads came up. I set the ask at 56.8, below the 6-heads value of 60.

{"bid": 30.0, "ask": 56.8}

Prior expected heads = 7 × (0.4×0.5 + 0.6×0.7) = 4.34, so fair value ≈ 43.4. The settlement standard deviation is about 14. Last quote's no-trade only says the value likely lies between 30 and 56.8, which leaves fair value near 43.4. I'm keeping a fairly wide spread because informed traders make up a large share and the value is still very uncertain.

{"bid": 35, "ask": 52}

Fair value is about 56.4. I quote a wide market around it: bid 46.5, ask 68.

**Posterior on the coin after three heads**
- Biased coin: 0.6 × 0.7³ = 0.2058.
- Fair coin: 0.4 × 0.5³ = 0.05.
- So P(biased) ≈ 0.80 and P(fair) ≈ 0.20.
- The expected heads probability is therefore about 0.661.

**Fair value**
- Three heads are already revealed, which is worth 30.
- The four remaining flips are expected to give about 2.64 more heads.
- Fair value ≈ 30 + 26.4 = 56.4.

**Settlement outcomes**

| Settlement | 30 | 40 | 50 | 60 | 70 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.02 | 0.11 | 0.29 | 0.38 | 0.21 |

**Choosing the quotes**
- I checked expected profit per quote against both informed traders and noise traders, whose noise has standard deviation 11.
- **Ask:** an ask in the high 60s means only the 70 outcome makes an informed trader buy. Noise buyers still give me some edge. Expected profit is about 0.9–1.0 at 66–69, so I post 68.
- **Bid:** expected profit peaks around 45–47, at about 0.8. I post 46.5.
- I am short one, so I am happy to buy back at that bid.

{"bid": 46.5, "ask": 68}

Fair value is about 56.4, so I'm quoting a wide spread around it: bid 46.0, ask 67.0.

**Fair value**
- Three heads in three flips raises the chance that this is the 0.7 coin. The likelihood is 0.343 for the 0.7 coin and 0.125 for the 0.5 coin.
- That moves P(0.7 coin) from 0.6 to about 0.80, so the expected heads rate is about 0.66 per flip.
- Settlement is expected at 10 × (3 + 4 × 0.661) ≈ 56.4. Last quote's no-trade adds little information.

**What the informed trader knows**
The settlement can only be 30, 40, 50, 60 or 70:

| Settlement | 70 | 60 | 50 | 40 | 30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.205 | 0.38 | 0.286 | 0.11 | 0.019 |

**Choosing each side**
- **Ask:** If the ask is above 60, the informed trader only buys when settlement is 70. My expected profit levels off at about 0.95 for an ask between 67 and 69. A tighter ask near 60 earns almost nothing.
- **Bid:** If the bid is below 50, the informed trader only sells when settlement is 40 or 30. My expected profit peaks at about 0.83 for a bid around 45 to 46.
- **Position:** I'm short 1, so there's no need to lean much either way.

{"bid": 46.0, "ask": 67.0}

Four heads so far make the high-bias coin much more likely, so fair value is about 60.1, and I'll quote 50 / 70.

**Which coin is it?**
- If P(heads) = 0.5, the chance of 4 heads in 4 flips is 0.0625. Weighted by its prior of 2/5, that gives 0.025.
- If P(heads) = 0.7, the chance is 0.2401. Weighted by its prior of 3/5, that gives 0.144.
- So the coin is 0.7 with probability about 0.852 and 0.5 with probability about 0.148.

**Fair value**
- The expected chance of heads on each remaining flip is 0.852 × 0.7 + 0.148 × 0.5 ≈ 0.670.
- Fair value is 40 + 3 × 6.70 ≈ 60.1. I don't adjust for the two earlier buys, though they hint slightly higher.

**Possible settlement values**

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 40 | 0.04 |
| 50 | 0.22 |
| 60 | 0.43 |
| 70 | 0.31 |

**Choosing the quotes**

I want each side to earn as much as possible from noise traders while losing little to informed traders.

- **Ask:** At 70, an informed trader never profits from buying, since settlement can't exceed 70. A noise trader buys about 18% of the time, for an expected edge of about 1.18 per quote. That is close to the best ask.
- **Bid:** At 50, an informed trader sells only when settlement is 40, which costs me little. A noise trader sells about 18% of the time. Net expected profit is about 1.0 per quote, which is near the best bid.

{"bid": 50, "ask": 70}

With 4 of 4 revealed flips heads, the coin is very likely the 0.7 coin. Fair value is about 60.1. I'm quoting a 50.0 bid and a 69.5 ask.

**Posterior on the coin.** The chance of four heads is 0.0625 for the fair coin and 0.2401 for the 0.7 coin. Weighting by the prior gives P(0.7 coin) ≈ 0.852. The expected chance of heads on each of the 3 unrevealed flips is therefore about 0.670.

**Fair value.** Expected heads are 4 + 3 × 0.670 ≈ 6.01, so fair value ≈ 60.1.

**Settlement distribution.**

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 40 | 0.042 |
| 50 | 0.217 |
| 60 | 0.431 |
| 70 | 0.311 |

**Ask.** An informed trader only buys when settlement is 70, which has probability 0.31. The loss to informed traders shrinks as the ask nears 70. The gain from noise traders (fair value plus Normal noise with standard deviation 11) is close to flat between 68 and 70. Expected edge per quote is about 1.1 at an ask of 69 to 69.5, about 1.0 at 68 and about 0.7 at 66. Even at 70 no informed trader buys and the edge is still about 1.18, so this is a flat maximum and 69.5 sits in it.

**Bid.** At 50, an informed trader only sells when settlement is 40, which has probability 0.04. Noise traders sell about 18% of the time at roughly 10 below fair. Expected edge is about 1.03, the best of the bids I checked.

{"bid": 50.0, "ask": 69.5}

Six heads have now been revealed, so the settlement is either 60 (flip 7 is tails) or 70 (flip 7 is heads). The questions are how likely heads is, and where to quote to profit from noise traders without losing to informed ones.

**How likely is the 0.7 coin?** Compare how well each coin explains six heads in a row, weighted by its starting probability:
- 0.7 coin: 0.6 × 0.7⁶ ≈ 0.0706
- 0.5 coin: 0.4 × 0.5⁶ = 0.00625

So the chance it is the 0.7 coin is 0.0706 / (0.0706 + 0.00625) ≈ 0.919.

**Fair value:**
- Chance flip 7 is heads = 0.919 × 0.7 + 0.081 × 0.5 ≈ 0.684.
- Fair value = 60 + 10 × 0.684 ≈ 66.8.

**Ask:**
- Any ask below 70 loses to informed traders whenever the value is 70.
- At 70 or above, only noise traders buy from me.
- Expected profit from noise buyers, by ask:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 70 | ≈ 0.80 |
| 74 | ≈ 1.20 |
| 75 | ≈ 1.22 (best) |
| 76 | ≈ 1.21 |

**Bid:**
- Any bid above 60 loses to informed traders whenever the value is 60.
- At 60 or below, only noise traders sell to me.
- Expected profit from noise sellers, by bid:

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 61 | ≈ 1.02 (after informed losses) |
| 60 | ≈ 1.19 |
| 59 | ≈ 1.21 (best) |
| 58 | ≈ 1.21 |

My position of −3 leaves room to trade one unit either way.

{"bid": 59, "ask": 75}

The contract settles at either 60 or 70, and fair value is about 66.84. I priced each side to maximise expected profit on this final quote.

**Posterior on the coin after 6 heads in 6 flips**
- Fair coin: 0.4 × 0.5⁶ = 0.00625
- Biased coin: 0.6 × 0.7⁶ ≈ 0.07059
- So P(biased coin) ≈ 0.9187.
- P(flip 7 is heads) ≈ 0.0813 × 0.5 + 0.9187 × 0.7 ≈ 0.684.
- Settlement is 70 with probability about 0.684 and 60 with probability about 0.316.
- Fair value ≈ 0.684 × 70 + 0.316 × 60 ≈ 66.84.

**Ask side**
- An informed trader buys only if its valuation is strictly above my ask. Its valuation is at most 70, so any ask of 70 or more is never hit by informed flow.
- Above 70, only noise traders buy. Expected profit is 0.65 × P(valuation > ask) × (ask − 66.84).
- Checking several asks, this peaks at about 1.21 around an ask of 75.5.

**Bid side**
- An informed trader sells only if its valuation is strictly below my bid. Its valuation is at least 60, so any bid of 60 or less is never hit by informed flow.
- At or below 60, only noise traders sell. Expected profit is 0.65 × P(valuation < bid) × (66.84 − bid).
- This is fairly flat between 58 and 60, at about 1.2, so I bid 58.5.

My position is −3, so a trade on either side keeps it within the ±5 limit. This is the last quote, so there is no future inventory risk to price in.

{"bid": 58.5, "ask": 75.5}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 2/5, P(heads) = 0.7 with probability 3/5. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 7 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 10 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Before any flips are seen, the expected chance of heads is 0.4×0.5 + 0.6×0.7 = 0.62. That makes the fair value 7 × 0.62 × 10 = 43.4.

The settlement value only takes multiples of 10, and its spread is about ±14. That is wide compared with the noise traders' ±11, so informed traders would hurt me on a tight quote. I compared candidate prices by expected profit per quote, combining the 0.65 chance of a noise trade with the 0.35 chance of losing to an informed trader:

| Quote | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| Bid 30.1 | about +0.48 |
| Bid 39.9 | about −0.59 |
| Ask 59.9 | about +0.53 |
| Ask 49.9 | about +0.20 |

The best choices sit just past the value steps, so an informed trader only trades when the value is far from my price. Bid 30.1 only fills against an informed seller when the value is 30 or less. Ask 59.9 only fills against an informed buyer when the value is 60 or more.

{"bid": 30.1, "ask": 59.9}

Quoting around a fair value of 43.4, with the bid 13 below and the ask 14 above.

**Fair value.** The expected chance of heads is 0.4×0.5 + 0.6×0.7 = 0.62. Over 7 flips that gives 4.34 expected heads, so the contract is worth about 43.4. The no-trade at the last quote barely changes this.

**Settlement spread.** The number of heads has a standard deviation of about 1.43 heads. That is about 14.3 points on the contract. The distribution leans to the right of 43.4:

| Heads | Probability | Settlement vs 43.4 |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 5% | +26.6 |
| 6 | 17% | +16.6 |
| 5 | 30% | +6.6 |
| 4 | 25% | −3.4 |
| 3 | 17% | −13.4 |
| 2 | 8% | −23.4 |
| 1 or 0 | 3% | −33 or worse |

**Choosing the gap.** For each gap from fair value, I compared two things. One is what I earn from noise traders (probability 0.65, noise standard deviation 11). The other is what I lose to informed traders (probability 0.35).

- **Ask side:** expected profit per quote is about +0.48 at a gap of 10, +0.55 at 13 and +0.53 at 16. The best is about 14 above fair, so the ask is 57.4.
- **Bid side:** expected profit per quote is about +0.37 at a gap of 10, +0.48 at 13 and +0.37 at 16. The best is about 13 below fair, so the bid is 30.4.

{"bid": 30.4, "ask": 57.4}

Fair value is about 52, taking both the revealed flips and the stage-1 trade into account.

**From the revealed flips (0, 1, 1):**
- If the coin is fair (P(heads) = 0.5), the chance of seeing 0, 1, 1 is 0.125. Times the prior of 0.4, that gives 0.05.
- If the coin is biased (P(heads) = 0.7), the chance is 0.147. Times the prior of 0.6, that gives 0.0882.
- So the updated chances are 0.362 for the fair coin and 0.638 for the biased coin.
- The expected chance of heads on each remaining flip is about 0.628.
- That gives 2 heads so far plus about 2.51 expected from the last 4 flips, so about 45 on the flips alone.

**From the trade history:**
- In stage 1 a counterparty bought at 57.4.
- An informed trader buys there only if the contract settles at 60 or more. Flip 1 was tails, so that needs all 4 remaining flips to be heads.
- A noise trader values the contract at about 43.4 plus noise. So the chance a noise trader buys at 57.4 is only about 10%.
- Before the trade, the chance of all 4 remaining flips being heads was about 0.176.
- Weighting by how likely a buy was in each case, that chance rises to about 0.58.
- If not all 4 are heads, the expected settlement is about 41.9. That gives an overall fair value of about 0.58 × 60 + 0.42 × 41.9 ≈ 52.

**The quote:**
- The settlement can only be a multiple of 10, and the top possible value is 60.
- An ask of 59 loses only 1 if an informed trader buys, and still earns against noise traders.
- I'm short 1, so I lean the quote slightly upward.
- A bid of 43 sits a little above 40, so informed sellers (settlement 40 or less) cost little.

{"bid": 43.0, "ask": 59.0}

Using the four revealed flips and the trading history, I estimate fair value at about 55–58, and I'm quoting a 52 bid and a 60 ask.

**Flips only:** three heads in four flips gives P(p=0.7) ≈ 0.71. That makes the expected heads probability about 0.642. The 3 remaining flips then add about 1.93 heads, for a fair value of about 49.3.

**Trading history:** two buys went through at 57.4 and 59, with no trade at 49/61. Informed buying is much more likely if the settlement is 60, meaning all remaining flips come up heads. A rough Bayesian update on the trades puts P(S=60) at about 0.8, which gives about 57.8. That probably overstates it, so I take fair value as roughly 55–58.

**Quote:**
- **Ask at 60:** the settlement can't exceed 60, so an informed trader never buys from me there. Any noise buy at 60 is profitable or break-even.
- **Bid at 52:** this lets me cover part of my short against noise sellers. The cost is a small loss if an informed trader sells when the settlement is 50.

{"bid": 52, "ask": 60}

I'm quoting a bid of 40 and an ask of 60, which is wide and centred on my fair value of about 49.3.

**Fair value.** The revealed flips show 3 heads in 4.
- How likely each coin is to produce that:
  - Fair coin (0.5): 0.5⁴ = 0.0625.
  - Biased coin (0.7): 0.7³ × 0.3 = 0.1029.
- After weighting by the prior, P(biased coin) = 0.712.
- The chance of heads on each remaining flip is then about 0.642.
- Fair value = 10 × (3 + 3 × 0.642) ≈ 49.3.

**Settlement distribution.** 3 flips remain, so settlement is 30, 40, 50 or 60.

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 30 | 0.055 |
| 40 | 0.243 |
| 50 | 0.422 |
| 60 | 0.280 |

**Ask.** Any ask at or above 60 means an informed trader never makes me lose on a buy. Noise traders still buy about 16% of the time, at roughly 10.7 above fair value. That works out to about +1.1 expected profit per quote, which is the best of the ask levels I checked.

**Bid.** At 40, an informed trader only sells to me when settlement is 30. That loses about 0.19 per quote. Noise traders sell about 20% of the time, at about 9.3 below fair value, which gains about 1.2. Raising the bid to 42 or 48 lets informed traders sell when settlement is 40 too, which costs more. Being short 2, a buy also reduces my risk.

{"bid": 40, "ask": 60}

Six flips are revealed and show 5 heads. The posterior on the 0.7 coin is about 0.83, so P(heads on flip 7) ≈ 0.666. Settlement is either 50 or 60, so the fair value is about 56.7.

- **Bid:** A bid at or below 50 is never hit by an informed trader. Expected profit from noise traders peaks around a bid of 48–49.
- **Ask:** An ask at or above 60 is never lifted by an informed trader. Expected profit from noise traders peaks around an ask of 64–65. Any ask below 60 has negative expected value, because informed traders who know the value is 60 would buy.

{"bid": 48.8, "ask": 64.2}

This is the last quote, and the contract can now only settle at 50 or 60, so I should set each side to maximise its own expected profit.

**Settlement value**
- Revealed flips show 5 heads in 6.
- The chance of those flips is (0.5)^6 ≈ 0.0156 for the fair coin and 0.7^5 × 0.3 ≈ 0.0504 for the biased coin.
- Weighting by the priors (2/5 and 3/5) gives P(biased coin | flips) ≈ 0.829.
- So P(flip 7 is heads) ≈ 0.171 × 0.5 + 0.829 × 0.7 ≈ 0.666.
- The contract settles at 60 with probability 0.666 and at 50 with probability 0.334. Fair value ≈ 56.66.

**Ask**
- At any ask of 60 or above, informed traders never buy: they only buy if their valuation is strictly above the ask, and the most it can be is 60.
- So above 60 only noise traders buy. Their valuation is 56.66 plus Normal noise with SD 11.
- Expected profit is roughly proportional to d × P(noise > d), where d is the ask minus 56.66. This peaks near d ≈ 0.75 × 11 ≈ 8.3.
- That gives an ask of about 65.0, worth about 0.65 × 0.227 × 8.3 ≈ 1.2.

**Bid**
- At any bid of 50 or below, informed traders never sell: their lowest possible valuation is 50, which is not below the bid.
- The same trade-off applies mirrored, so the best bid is about 56.66 − 8.3 ≈ 48.3.

**Position**
- I am short 3. Selling one more would take me to −4, which is within the limit, so both sides can be quoted.

{"bid": 48.3, "ask": 65.0}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 7/10, P(heads) = 0.7 with probability 3/10. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 5 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Fair value is about 17.2. With no trade at 12.6/21, the most likely settlements are now 15 and 20 (3 or 4 heads). That pushes informed traders toward the middle, so wide quotes just inside 25 and just above 5 maximise expected profit from noise traders while limiting losses to informed ones.

**Prior.** The expected chance of heads is 0.7·0.5 + 0.3·0.7 = 0.56. That gives 6 × 0.56 = 3.36 expected heads, so the starting fair value is 16.8.

**Update from the first quote.** Nobody traded at 12.6 / 21.
- An informed trader would not trade only if the value were 15 or 20.
- A noise trader would not trade with probability of about 0.33.
- So settlements of 15 or 20 are now relatively more likely, and fair value rises to about 17.2.
- Updated probabilities: about 48% that the value is 20 or more, about 8% that it is 25 or more, and about 3% that it is 5 or less.

**Ask.**
- An ask just under 20 gets picked off by informed traders about 48% of the time.
- An ask just under 25 is only exposed when the value is 25 or 30 (about 8%).
- Noise traders still buy there about 22% of the time, earning about 7.7 above fair value.
- Expected profit on this side is about 0.79 per quote, close to the best available.

**Bid.**
- A bid at 10.0 is only exposed when the value is 0 or 5 (about 3%).
- Noise traders sell there about 23% of the time, about 7.2 below fair value.
- Expected profit on this side is about 0.75 per quote.

{"bid": 10.0, "ask": 24.9}

I'm quoting a wide spread, roughly symmetric around fair value, with each side just outside a possible settlement value.

**Fair value.** Each flip is heads with probability 0.7·0.5 + 0.3·0.7 = 0.56. That gives an expected 3.36 heads, so the contract is worth about 16.8. The two quotes with no trade only shift this a little, towards 15 to 20.

**Settlement values.** The contract can only settle at 0, 5, 10, …, 30. Weighting the fair coin at 0.7 and the biased coin at 0.3 gives these probabilities for the number of heads:

| Heads | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.011 | 0.069 | 0.182 | 0.274 | 0.261 | 0.156 | 0.046 |

**Ask at 25.0.**
- An informed trader only buys if the value is 30 (above my ask, not equal to it). That costs about 0.5 × 0.046 × 5 ≈ 0.12.
- Noise traders buy about 21% of the time, earning about 8 each time, which is worth about 0.84 before weighting.
- Net, the ask is worth about +0.72 per quote, the best of the ask prices I checked.

**Bid at 9.9.**
- Bidding just under 10 means an informed trader at value 10 does not sell to me.
- Informed traders sell only at values 0 or 5, which costs about 0.22.
- Noise traders sell about 24% of the time, which is worth about 0.83.
- Net, the bid is worth about +0.61.

{"bid": 9.9, "ask": 25.0}

Fair value: after flip 1 = heads, the chance the coin is the 0.7-heads coin rises to 0.375. That puts the expected heads probability on each remaining flip at 0.575. Expected value = 5 × (1 + 5 × 0.575) ≈ 19.4.

The no-trade history from stage 1 tells us little, because those quotes were wide.

The settlement value can only be 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 or 30. Its probabilities are about 0.02, 0.11, 0.25, 0.31, 0.23 and 0.08.

For each side I compared the expected loss to informed traders with the expected gain from noise traders (standard deviation 9.9):
- **Ask:** about 29 is best. Only an informed trader holding a value of 30 buys there, and the noise-trader edge is about 0.76 per quote.
- **Bid:** 10.0 is best. Only an informed trader holding a value of 5 sells there, and the noise-trader edge is about 0.76 per quote.

{"bid": 10.0, "ask": 29.0}

After flip 1 = 1, the posterior that the coin is the biased one is 0.21 / 0.56 = 0.375. That makes the expected heads probability 0.575. The expected settlement is 5 × (1 + 5 × 0.575) ≈ 19.4. The earlier quotes produced no trades, so they don't move this.

The settlement can only be 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 or 30. Its probabilities are about 2%, 11%, 24%, 31%, 23% and 8%.

**Ask:** Placing the ask just under 30 means an informed buyer only costs me money when the value is 30 (about 8%), and then I lose little. Noise buyers still pay well above fair value. An ask near 29 gives the best expected profit, about 0.76 per quote.

**Bid:** Placing the bid just under 10 means an informed seller only costs me money when the value is 5 (about 2%). Noise sellers still sell well below fair value. A bid near 9.9–10.5 gives the best expected profit, about 0.75 per quote.

{"bid": 9.9, "ask": 29}

Bid 10 and ask 29.5, which keeps both sides wide.

**Fair value**
- Seeing flip 1 = heads updates the odds on the coin. For the fair coin, prior 0.7 × likelihood 0.5 gives 0.35. For the biased coin, 0.3 × 0.7 gives 0.21.
- The posterior is therefore 0.625 for the fair coin and 0.375 for the biased coin. The expected chance of heads is now 0.575.
- Five flips are still unknown, so expected heads = 1 + 5 × 0.575 = 3.875. Fair value is 5 × 3.875 = **19.4**.
- The earlier quotes drew no trades and were wide, so the trading history tells us nothing new.

**Settlement distribution** (k = heads in the remaining five flips; settlement value = 5 + 5k)

| Value | 5 | 10 | 15 | 20 | 25 | 30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.020 | 0.108 | 0.245 | 0.311 | 0.233 | 0.083 |

**Choosing the quotes**
- Each candidate quote is scored by two things. One is the expected loss to an informed trader, who trades only when the true value is beyond our price. The other is the expected profit from a noise trader, whose valuation is 19.4 plus noise with standard deviation 9.9.
- On the ask side, the net expected profit rises from about 0.37 at 24 to about 0.76 at 29–30. It is essentially flat above 29.
- On the bid side, a bid of 10 nets about 0.75. A bid of 12 nets only about 0.66, and one of 15 about 0.35, because informed sellers then also catch us when the value is 10.
- The best quotes are therefore far from fair value on both sides.

{"bid": 10, "ask": 29.5}

I'm quoting bid 13.3 and ask 28.3, about 7.5 either side of fair value.

**Fair value.** Flips 1–4 show 3 heads and 1 tail.
- The chance of that pattern is 0.0625 for the fair coin and 0.1029 for the biased coin.
- Weighting by the 7/10 and 3/10 priors, the chance the coin is the biased one is about 0.414.
- Expected P(heads) for each remaining flip is 0.5 + 0.2 × 0.414 ≈ 0.583.
- Expected total heads is 3 + 2 × 0.583 ≈ 4.17, so fair value ≈ 20.83.

**Possible settlement values.** With 3 heads already, settlement is 15, 20 or 25.

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 15 | about 0.18 |
| 20 | about 0.47 |
| 25 | about 0.35 |

**Ask.** If the ask is above 25, an informed trader never buys, so only noise traders hit it. Expected profit is then 0.5 × P(noise buys) × (ask − 20.83). This peaks when the ask is about 0.75 standard deviations above fair, roughly 7.5 points, giving an ask of about 28.3. Expected profit there is about 0.84 per quote.

**Bid.** The same logic applies on the other side. With the bid at or below 15, an informed trader never sells. The best spot is about 7.5 below fair, roughly 13.3.

{"bid": 13.3, "ask": 28.3}

The fair value is about 20.8, so I'm quoting a bid of 13.4 and an ask of 28.3, placed outside the possible settlement values. That way informed traders never trade with me and I only collect edge from noise traders.

**Posterior on the coin.** Flips 1–4 show 3 heads and 1 tail.
- Probability of this result with a fair coin: 0.5⁴ = 0.0625. Weighted by the 0.7 prior: 0.04375.
- Probability with the biased coin: 0.7³ × 0.3 = 0.1029. Weighted by the 0.3 prior: 0.03087.
- So P(biased) = 0.03087 / (0.04375 + 0.03087) ≈ 0.414.
- Expected P(heads) = 0.5 + 0.2 × 0.414 ≈ 0.583.

**Settlement distribution.** The 2 unrevealed flips decide the result.
- 0 more heads, settles at 15: probability ≈ 0.184
- 1 more head, settles at 20: probability ≈ 0.467
- 2 more heads, settles at 25: probability ≈ 0.349
- Fair value ≈ 15 + 5 × 2 × 0.583 ≈ 20.83.

**Ask.** If the ask is above 25, informed traders never buy from me.
- Against noise traders, the expected edge is P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 20.83). This is largest at about 0.75σ above fair, which is an ask of about 28.3.
- The expected value per quote is about 0.5 × 0.227 × 7.47 ≈ 0.85.
- For comparison, an ask of 25 gives about 0.70, and an ask of 24 gives about 0.42.

**Bid.** The same logic applies on the other side.
- A bid below 15 means informed traders never sell to me.
- The best bid is about 20.83 − 7.4 ≈ 13.4, with an expected value of about 0.84.
- A bid of 17 gives only about 0.48, because informed traders sell to me when the settlement is 15.

{"bid": 13.4, "ask": 28.3}

This is the last quote, so I only need the best one-shot expected profit on each side.

**Posterior on the coin.** The revealed flips are 1, 0, 1, 1, which is 3 heads and 1 tail.
- Fair coin: prior 0.7 × 0.5⁴ = 0.04375.
- Biased coin (0.7): prior 0.3 × 0.7³ × 0.3 = 0.03087.
- So P(biased) ≈ 0.414 and P(fair) ≈ 0.586.

**Settlement distribution.** The settlement is 5 × (3 + heads in flips 5 and 6).
- P(settles at 15, no more heads) ≈ 0.184
- P(settles at 20, one more head) ≈ 0.467
- P(settles at 25, two more heads) ≈ 0.349
- Public fair value ≈ 20.83.

**Ask side.** Any ask at 25 or above can never be hit by an informed trader at a loss to me, since one only buys if its valuation is strictly above the ask. Against noise traders alone, expected profit is the edge d times the chance a noise trader's valuation exceeds fair value plus d. That product, d × P(noise > d), peaks at about d ≈ 0.75σ ≈ 7.4. This gives an ask of about 28.3. Asks between 20 and 25 earn more noise volume but lose to informed buyers when it settles at 25, and come out worse.

**Bid side.** By the same logic, the bid is about 20.83 − 7.4 ≈ 13.4. This is below 15, so informed sellers never hit it. I checked a bid of 16: it earns about 0.76 from noise traders but loses about 0.09 to informed sellers, so it is worse than 13.4.

{"bid": 13.4, "ask": 28.3}

game.title: Coin of unknown bias
game.description: A coin is picked at random from a set of coins: P(heads) = 0.5 with probability 7/10, P(heads) = 0.7 with probability 3/10. The coin is not shown. It is flipped 6 times. Revealed flips show 1 for heads and 0 for tails.
game.contract: The contract settles at 5 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Before any flips are revealed, the fair value is about 16.8. The expected chance of heads is 0.7×0.5 + 0.3×0.7 = 0.56, so the expected number of heads is 6 × 0.56 = 3.36, worth 3.36 × 5 = 16.8.

The settlement can only be a multiple of 5. Its rough probabilities are:

| Heads | Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 1.1% |
| 1 | 5 | 6.9% |
| 2 | 10 | 18.2% |
| 3 | 15 | 27.4% |
| 4 | 20 | 26.1% |
| 5 | 25 | 15.6% |
| 6 | 30 | 4.6% |

Counterparties only trade when their valuation is strictly beyond my price. So quoting exactly on a possible settlement value means an informed trader holding that value does not trade.

I compared three quotes by expected profit per step:

| Bid / Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 15 / 25 | about +0.2 |
| 10 / 20 | about +0.6 |
| 10 / 25 | about +1.3 |

At 10 / 25, informed traders only hit me when the settlement is 5 or below, or 30. That costs about 0.7 on average when they trade. Noise traders hit either side about 20–25% of the time, with an edge of about 7–8, earning about 3.3 on average when they trade. Each type arrives half the time, which gives the +1.3.

{"bid": 10.0, "ask": 25.0}

Before any reveals, the chance of heads is 0.7×0.5 + 0.3×0.7 = 0.56. So expected heads are 6 × 0.56 = 3.36, and the fair value is about 16.8. The 10/25 quote that didn't trade barely changes that estimate.

The settlement value is always a multiple of 5. That means an informed trader only hits my bid or lifts my ask when the true value is past the next multiple of 5, which limits how much I lose to them. Noise traders' valuations are spread with a standard deviation of 9.9 around 16.8, so a wide quote still catches a fair share of them.

I compared the expected profit of different quotes, weighing gains from noise traders against losses to informed traders:
- **Ask:** about 26 does best. Informed traders only buy when the value is 30, which happens about 4.6% of the time. Expected profit on that side is about 0.72.

game.contract: The contract settles at 5 times the number of heads in all flips.

info.raw:
Pre-reveal fair value: expected P(heads) = 0.2·0.2 + 0.3·0.7 + 0.5·0.9 = 0.70. That gives 3.5 expected heads, so the contract is worth 5 × 3.5 = **17.5**.

I quote 4 either side of fair, at 13.5 / 21.5. Noise traders have a valuation spread of 12, so each side should earn about 1.18 per quote from them. The edge given up to informed traders is smaller:
- **Ask at 21.5:** an informed trader buys only if the coin shows 5 heads (settles at 25), which has probability about 0.35. Expected cost is about 0.24.
- **Bid at 13.5:** an informed trader sells only if there are 2 or fewer heads, which has probability about 0.24. Expected cost is about 0.36.

Both sides have positive expected value at this width.

{"bid": 13.5, "ask": 21.5}

**Fair value after the first trade.** Before any trading, the expected chance of heads is 0.2·0.2 + 0.3·0.7 + 0.5·0.9 = 0.70. So the expected settlement is 25 × 0.70 = 17.5.

At 21.5, an informed trader only buys if all 5 flips are heads (settlement 25).
- The prior chance of 5 heads is about 0.346.
- A noise trader buys at 21.5 with probability P(Z > 0.33), about 0.37.
- So the chance of a buy is 0.2 + 0.8 × 0.37 ≈ 0.495 if all 5 are heads, and ≈ 0.295 otherwise.
- After the buy, the chance of 5 heads rises to about 0.47.
- If not all heads, the expected settlement is about 13.5.
- The new public fair value is 0.47 × 25 + 0.53 × 13.5 ≈ 18.9.

**Quote.** Settlement values are multiples of 5.
- With the ask at 22, informed traders still only buy when settlement is 25.
- With the bid at 14.8, informed traders only sell when settlement is 10 or less.

I'm short 1, so I lean the quote slightly toward buying.

Public fair value is about 21.1, after updating on flip 1 = heads and on the trading history.

**Flip 1 alone**

- The expected heads probability for the remaining four flips is 0.8.
- So the expected settlement is 5 × (1 + 4 × 0.8) = 21.

**Distribution of the settlement value**
Value = 5 × (1 + heads in flips 2–5). Mixing over the three coins:

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 25 | 0.494 |
| 20 | 0.312 |
| 15 | 0.119 |
| 10 | 0.048 |
| 5 | 0.026 |

- Expected profit from noise traders on one side is (distance from fair) × P(noise valuation is beyond that distance), times 0.8. With noise SD 12 this peaks at roughly 9 away from fair, and the curve is flat near the peak.
